RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r1.claim: The quoted poetic example treats uttering only the letter qāf as a saying or statement.

RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r2.claim: Qawl can stand metaphorically for beliefs and doctrines: saying someone follows Abu Ḥanīfa or Mālik means adopting their beliefs; calling a denial of vision the Muʿtazila’s qawl is apt, while kalām would be strained.
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r2.anchor: لفظ القول يصح جعله مجازا عن الاعتقادات والآراء

RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r3.claim: Qāla may describe nonverbal expression: poets make birds, eyes, and a full water trough “speak,” as do the Qurʾānic commands to creation to say “Be” and to heaven and earth to come.
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r3.anchor: لفظ قال قد يستعمل في غير النطق

RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r4.speaker: الذين ينكرون كلام النفس
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r4.claim: Those who deny inner speech hold that kalām and qawl name only spoken words and uttered expressions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r4.anchor: الذين ينكرون كلام النفس اتفقوا على أن الكلام والقول اسم لهذه الألفاظ والكلمات

RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r5.speaker: مثبتو كلام النفس
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r5.claim: Proponents of inner speech say the inward mental meaning is also called kalām and qawl, citing the Qurʾānic description of the hypocrites as liars.
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r5.anchor: أما مثبتو كلام النفس فقد اتفقوا على أن ذلك المعنى النفساني يسمى بالكلام وبالقول واحتجوا عليه بالقرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r6.claim: Razi rejects that proof: the hypocrites lied in claiming to bear witness, since testimony requires knowledge and they lacked it, even though Muhammad is truly God's messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r6.anchor: الشهادة لا تحصل إلا مع العلم وهم ما كانوا عالمين به فثبت أنهم كانوا كاذبين فيما أخبروا عنه بالقول اللساني

RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r7.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r7.claim: At the Saqīfa, ʿUmar said he had prepared words inwardly, but Abū Bakr spoke before him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r7.anchor: ما نقل أن عمر قال يوم السقيفة

STUDYQURAN:3:35/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:35/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:35/r1.claim: Idh attaches to what precedes and is commonly construed with the implied imperative udhkur, meaning remember or mention.
STUDYQURAN:3:35/r1.anchor: the Arabic particle idh, which indicates attachment to something that has preceded. In this instance it is said to be related, as is often the case, to the implied injunction udhkur

STUDYQURAN:3:35/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:35/r2.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:3:35/r2.claim: Mary's father ʿImrān reportedly died before her birth; her mother Ḥannah vowed to dedicate the child to Temple service, study, and worship without other duties.
STUDYQURAN:3:35/r2.anchor: It is reported that Mary’s father, ʿImrān, died before she was born, and her mother, Ḥannah (Anne), promised to dedicate her child to the service of the Temple

TAB-FULL:v5p330/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r1.claim: Ṭabarī says إذ in the opening clause is syntactically connected to السميع in the preceding context.
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r1.anchor: السميع لما أقول وأدعو، العليم لما أنوي في نفسي

TAB-FULL:v5p330/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r2.claim: The woman of Imran is Mary’s mother, mother of Jesus; Ṭabarī gives her name as Hanna daughter of Faqudh son of Qatil, with another spelling Faqud.
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r2.anchor: وكان اسمها فيما ذكر لنا حنة ابنة فاقوذ بن قتيل

TAB-FULL:v5p330/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq gives Imran’s lineage as son of Yashham, through the listed ancestors, down to Solomon, David, and Jesse.

TAB-FULL:v5p330/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r4.claim: Ṭabarī explains that she vowed the unborn child to God, setting the child apart for worship and service of the sanctuary, free from all other service and worldly use.
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r4.anchor: حبسته على خدمتك وخدمة قدسك في الكنيسة عتيقة من خدمة كل شيء سواك، مفرغة لك خاصة

TAB-FULL:v5p330/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r5.claim: Ṭabarī parses محررا as a circumstantial accusative modifying ما, understood as الذي.
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r5.anchor: ونصب «محررا» على الحال من «ما» التي بمعنى

TAB-FULL:v5p330/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r6.claim: The mother asks God to accept the child she has vowed.
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r6.anchor: أي فتقبل مني ما نذرت لك يا رب

TAB-FULL:v5p330/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r7.claim: God hears her words and prayer and knows her inward intention and desire, with nothing hidden from Him, inwardly or outwardly.
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r7.anchor: السميع لما أقول وأدعو، العليم لما أنوي في نفسي وأريد، لا يخفى عليك سر أمري وعلانيته

TAB-FULL:v5p330/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r8.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts that Zechariah and Imran married sisters, Imran died while Mary’s mother was pregnant, and she had long seemed unable to bear a child; seeing a bird feed its chick stirred her to pray, and after conceiving Mary she vowed the child to church service without worldly use.
TAB-FULL:v5p330/r8.anchor: محمد بن إسحاق، قال: " تزوج زكريا وعمران أختين، فكانت أم يحيى عند زكريا، وكانت أم مريم عند عمران، فهلك عمران وأم مريم حامل بمريم

TAB-FULL:v5p335/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r1.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr glosses the vow as dedicating the child, free for worship of God and unavailable for worldly affairs.
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير، قال: ثم ذكر امرأة عمران، وقولها: {رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا} [آل عمران: 35] أي نذرته

TAB-FULL:v5p335/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r2.claim: Mujahid says the child was to serve the church or monastery.
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {محررا} [آل عمران: 35] قال: «خادما للبيعة»

TAB-FULL:v5p335/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r3.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi explains the vow as setting the child apart for worship in the church.
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي، في قوله: {إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا} [آل عمران: 35] قال: «فرغته للعبادة»

TAB-FULL:v5p335/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r4.claim: Mujahid also says the child was made wholly devoted, with no worldly matter mixed into the dedication.
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: {إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا} [آل عمران: 35] قال: «خالصا لا يخالطه شيء من أمر الدنيا»

TAB-FULL:v5p335/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the child was dedicated to the church and worship.
TAB-FULL:v5p335/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: {إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا} [آل عمران: 35] قال: «للبيعة والكنيسة»

TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r1.claim: Qatadah says the mother consecrated the unborn child to God; since such offerings were usually male, a boy would stay in the church to tend and clean it.
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إذ قالت امرأة عمران رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا} [آل عمران: 35] الآية، «كانت امرأة عمران حررت لله ما في بطنها

TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says she assumed she carried a boy and dedicated him to God as free from worldly work.
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي: {إذ قالت امرأة عمران رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا فتقبل مني إنك أنت السميع العليم} [آل عمران: 35] قال: «وذلك أن امرأة عمران حملت

TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says offerings were usually male and the consecrated boy stayed in the church to care for and sweep it.
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r3.anchor: عن الربيع، قال: " كانت امرأة عمران حررت لله ما في بطنها، قال: وكانوا إنما يحررون الذكور

TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says she dedicated her child to God and to those who study and learn the Book.
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، في قوله: {إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا}

TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة وأبو بكر
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r5.claim: Ikrimah’s account says the barren elderly Hanna vowed, in gratitude for a child, to give the child to the Temple as a keeper and servant; محرر means a free child dedicated to church service.
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r5.anchor: عن القاسم بن أبي بزة، أنه أخبره عن عكرمة، وأبي بكر، عن عكرمة: " أن امرأة عمران كانت عجوزا عاقرا تسمى حنة، وكانت لا تلد

TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says she vowed the child in her womb and then released her.
TAB-FULL:v5p335#2/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {إذ قالت امرأة عمران} [آل عمران: 35] الآية كلها، قال: «نذرت ما في بطنها ثم سيبتها»

TABATABAI:3:35-36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r1.claim: A vow is a person's making obligatory upon himself something that was not obligatory.
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r1.anchor: النذر إيجاب الإنسان على نفسه ما ليس بواجب

TABATABAI:3:35-36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r2.claim: Taḥrīr means release from a bond, as in freeing a slave or “releasing” meanings from the mind in writing.
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r2.anchor: والتحرير هو الإطلاق عن وثاق ومنه تحرير العبد عن الرقية وتحرير الكتاب

TABATABAI:3:35-36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r3.claim: Taqabbul is acceptance with willingness and approval, like accepting a gift or a prayer.
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r3.anchor: والتقبل هو القبول عن رغبة ورضى كتقبل الهدية وتقبل الدعاء ونحو ذلك

TABATABAI:3:35-36/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r4.claim: Her wording indicates she spoke while pregnant and that Imran was the father; the passage hints he had died, since otherwise she could not independently dedicate the unborn child, as 3:44 also suggests.
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r4.anchor: دلالة على أنها إنما قالت هذا القول حينما كانت حاملا وأن حملها كان من عمران

TABATABAI:3:35-36/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r5.claim: A parent's dedication does not manumit a child; it releases the child from parental guardianship and use for the parents' aims, placing the child under God's authority for worship and service.
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r5.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن تحرير الأب أو الأم للولد ليس تحريرا عن الرقية وإنما هو تحرير عن قيد الولاية التي للوالدين

TABATABAI:3:35-36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r6.claim: A reported custom was to dedicate a child to God for church service and cleaning until puberty, then let the child choose to stay or leave.
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r6.anchor: وقد قيل إنهم كانوا يحررون الولد لله فكان الأبوان لا يستعملانه في منافعهما

TABATABAI:3:35-36/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r7.claim: She believed the unborn child was male: her vow is unconditional, and the masculine “dedicated” is not merely agreement with the gender-neutral “what”; otherwise her grief at a girl and the later contrast would be unexplained.
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r7.anchor: وفي الكلام دلالة على أنها كانت تعتقد أن ما في بطنها ذكر لا إناث حيث إنها تناجي ربها عن جزم وقطع

TABATABAI:3:35-36/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r8.claim: Her certainty was not a guess based on women's intuition: God's narration does not leave falsehood uncorrected, so her firm claim about the womb had a truthful basis.
TABATABAI:3:35-36/r8.anchor: اعتقادها ذلك لم يكن عن جزاف أو اعتمادا على بعض القرائن الحدسية التي تسبق إلى أذهان النسوان

TABATABAI:3:36-37/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:36-37/r1.claim: Since the fetus's sex belongs to God's unseen knowledge (13:8; 31:34), and knowledge of the unseen reaches others through revelation (72:26), Mary's certainty about a son must have been revealed.
TABATABAI:3:36-37/r1.anchor: فجعل العلم بما في الأرحام من الغيب المختص به تعالى وقال تعالى عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا إلا من ارتضى

TABATABAI:3:36-37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:36-37/r3.claim: The object of “accept from me” is omitted and could be either her vow or the consecrated child; 3:37's “accepted her” suggests she meant acceptance of the child.
TABATABAI:3:36-37/r3.anchor: نذرها من حيث إنه عمل صالح أو يكون هو ولدها المحرر

TABATABAI:3:35-41#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#5/r1.claim: Inner promptings are called commands, speech, whispering, inspiration, or promises, yet they are meanings cast into hearts rather than words uttered by mouth and tongue.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#5/r1.anchor: سميت بالأمر والقول والوسوسة والوحي والوعد وجميعها قول وكلام ولم تخرج عن شق فم ولا تحريك لسان

TABATABAI:3:35-41#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#5/r2.claim: The inward speech of angels and devils is another mode of communication; God alone also speaks to people through revelation or from behind a veil.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#5/r2.anchor: وهنا قسم آخر من التكليم يختص به تعالى كما ذكره بقوله وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا

TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r1.claim: Divine revelation has no veil between God and the person addressed, so it cannot be confused; other communication needs confirmation that ultimately goes back to revelation.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r1.anchor: فهو تكليم حيث لا حجاب بين الإنسان وبين ربه، ومن المحال أن يقع هناك لبس وهو ظاهر

TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r2.claim: An angelic prompting opens the heart, urges forgiveness and generosity, and accords with scripture and prophetic practice; satanic prompting constricts it, urges desire and indecency, and conflicts with revelation and human nature.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r2.anchor: الخاطر الملكي يصاحب انشراح الصدر، ويدعو إلى المغفرة والفضل وينتهي بالآخرة إلى ما يطابق دين الله المبين

TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r3.claim: Prophets and their followers may recognize angels and devils by seeing them; when they cannot see them, they must discern inward promptings as other believers do, ultimately distinguishing revelation.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r3.anchor: ربما تيسر لهم مشاهدة الملك والشيطان ومعرفتهما كما حكى الله تعالى عن آدم وإبراهيم ولوط

TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r4.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r4.claim: Al-Qummi reports from Imam al-Sadiq that God told Imran he would have a virtuous son, a miracle-working messenger; Imran told Hanna, who expected a boy, while Jesus later fulfilled the promise through Mary.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#6/r4.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام قال إن الله أوحى إلى عمران أني واهب لك ذكرا سويا مباركا يبرئ الأكمه

TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r1.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r1.claim: A report in al-Ayyashi says a consecrated child remains in the sanctuary; a girl menstruates and must leave it, explaining the mother's remark that a boy is unlike a girl.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r1.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام أن المحرر يكون في الكنيسة لا يخرج منها فلما وضعتها قالت

TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r2.speaker: أحدهما
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r2.claim: Another report says the child was vowed to serve worshippers; Mary served them until she grew up, when Zakariya was ordered to put a screen between her and the worshippers.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r2.anchor: وفيه عن أحدهما نذرت ما في بطنها للكنيسة أن يخدم العباد وليس الذكر كالأنثى في الخدمة

TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r7.claim: Some commentators object that the reports about revelation to Imran, Mary's out-of-season fruit, and Zakariya's request for a sign lack support from scripture, the Prophet, reason, or reliable history.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r7.anchor: بعض المفسرين شدد النكير على ما تضمنته هذه الروايات كالوحي إلى عمران ووجود الفاكهة في محراب مريم

TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i answers that the dismissal is unargued: although solitary reports with weak chains need not be accepted as proof, reflection on the verses makes the Ahl al-Bayt reports plausible and none is irrational.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r1.anchor: وهو منه كلام من غير حجة والروايات وإن كانت آحادا غير خالية عن ضعف الطريق لا يجب على الباحث الأخذ بها

TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r4.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r4.claim: Al-Kafi reports from Imam al-Sadiq that every heart has an angel who guides and a satan who tempts: Satan urges sins while the angel restrains them; the report applies 50:18 to this presence.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r4.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام ما من قلب إلا وله أذنان على إحداهما ملك مرشد وعلى الأخرى شيطان مفتن

TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r5.claim: This application of the watcher at a person's right and left does not exclude the report that the watchers are recording angels, since the verse does not specify their identity.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r5.anchor: لا ينافي تطبيقه إياها على الملكين الكاتبين للحسنات والسيئات في رواية أخرى فإن الآية لا تدل على أزيد من وجود رقيب عتيد

TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r6.speaker: زرارة عن أبي عبد الله
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r6.claim: Al-Kafi reports from Imam al-Sadiq that a messenger sees the angel bearing God's message and may also be a prophet; a prophet receives revelation in the heart without seeing the angel, and God makes him know a dream is true.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r6.anchor: عن زرارة قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن الرسول وعن النبي وعن المحدث قال الرسول الذي يعاين الملك

TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r7.claim: The report says messenger and prophet can be combined in one person, which al-Tabataba'i connects to his earlier discussion of prophecy and messengership.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r7.anchor: والرسول يكون نبيا إشارة إلى إمكان اجتماع الوصفين وقد تقدم الكلام في معنى الرسالة والنبوة

TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r1.speaker: بريد عن الباقر والصادق عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r1.claim: Al-Basa'ir reports that a messenger sees the angel, a prophet receives revelation in a dream, and a muḥaddath hears a voice without seeing its form; God enables recognition of a true dream, and the report says the Qur'an and Muhammad seal earlier books and prophets.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r1.anchor: عن بريد عن الباقر والصادق عليهما السلام في حديث قال بريد فما الرسول والنبي والمحدث

TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r2.claim: The report's phrase that God clarifies the dream refers to distinguishing true angelic input from satanic input by the truth God makes clear.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r2.anchor: إشارة إلى التمييز بين الإلقاء الملكي والشيطاني بما بينه الله من الحق

TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r3.claim: The report explains the muḥaddath as someone who hears a caller's voice without seeing its form.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#9/r3.anchor: وبيانه عليه السلام واف بتمييز المحدث ما يسمعه من صوت الهاتف

TABRISI:3:35-36/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:35-36/r2.claim: Muḥarrar can mean freed from servitude, or purified and corrected as a text is when edited.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r2.anchor: معنى المحرر في اللغة يحتمل أمرين

TABRISI:3:35-36/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:35-36/r3.claim: To accept is to receive something willingly; its root sense is reciprocation, as in accepting a gift.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r3.anchor: والتقبل أخذ الشيء على الرضا به كتقبل الهدية وأصل التقبل المقابلة

TABRISI:3:35-36/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:35-36/r4.claim: Waḍʿ means putting down; a woman’s putting down her child means giving birth, and related forms mean place, lowliness, or easing one’s pace.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r4.anchor: وأصل الوضع الحط وضعت المرأة الولد بمعنى ولدت

TABRISI:3:35-36/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r5.speaker: الأخفش والمبرد
TABRISI:3:35-36/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad parse idh as an object governed by an implied remember.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r5.anchor: أنه نصب بأذكر عن الأخفش والمبرد

TABRISI:3:35-36/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:3:35-36/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj connects idh to God’s choosing the family of ʿImrān.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r6.anchor: أنه متعلق باصطفى آل عمران عن الزجاج

TABRISI:3:35-36/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r7.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:3:35-36/r7.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā connects idh to the attributes All-Hearing and All-Knowing, whose sense encompasses her speech and intention.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r7.anchor: أنه متعلق بسميع عليم فيعمل فيه معنى الصفتين تقديره والله مدرك لقولها ونيتها إذ قالت عن علي بن عيسى

TABRISI:3:35-36/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:3:35-36/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats idh as extra and unparsed; the author notes that Basran grammarians consider this wrong.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r8.anchor: أن إذ زائدة فلا موضع لها من الإعراب عن أبي عبيدة وهذا خطأ عند البصريين

TABRISI:3:35-36/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:35-36/r9.claim: Muḥarraran is a circumstantial accusative describing what was in her womb, governed by her vow.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r9.anchor: ومحررا نصب على الحال من ما وتقديره نذرت لك الذي في بطني محررا

TABRISI:3:35-36/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:35-36/r11.claim: The wife of ʿImrān is named Ḥanna, Mary’s grandmother; authorities differ whether her husband was ʿImrān ibn al-Hāshim or ʿImrān ibn Māthān, not Moses’ father, who lived eighteen centuries earlier.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r11.anchor: واسمها حنة جدة عيسى وكانتا أختين

TABRISI:3:35-36/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r12.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
TABRISI:3:35-36/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil identify ʿImrān as Ibn Māthān and say the two sisters married ʿImrān and Zechariah; Yaḥyā and Mary were maternal cousins.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r12.anchor: وقيل هو عمران بن ماثان عن ابن عباس ومقاتل وليس بعمران أبي موسى

TABRISI:3:35-36/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:35-36/r13.claim: Ḥanna obligates herself to dedicate the child in her womb to God’s service.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r13.anchor: أي أوجبت لك بأن أجعل ما في بطني

TABRISI:3:35-36/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r14.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:3:35-36/r14.claim: Mujāhid understands the vow as dedicating the child to serve the sanctuary and its places of worship.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r14.anchor: أي خادما للبيعة يخدم في متعبداتنا عن مجاهد

TABRISI:3:35-36/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r15.speaker: الشعبي
TABRISI:3:35-36/r15.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the child was freed for worship and devoted exclusively to it.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r15.anchor: محررا للعبادة مخلصا لها عن الشعبي

TABRISI:3:35-36/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r16.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
TABRISI:3:35-36/r16.claim: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says the child was freed for obedience to God, not used for personal benefits or needs.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r16.anchor: عتيقا خالصا لطاعتك لا استعمله في منافعي ولا أصرفه في الحوائج عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير

TABRISI:3:35-36/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:35-36/r17.claim: Those dedicated to the sanctuary served and cleaned it until puberty, then could stay or leave.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r17.anchor: وكان المحرر إذا حرر جعل في الكنيسة يقوم عليها ويكنسها ويخدمها

TABRISI:3:35-36/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r18.speaker: قالوا
TABRISI:3:35-36/r18.claim: They say Ḥanna had despaired of having a child; seeing a bird feed its chick under a tree stirred her desire, so she prayed and conceived Mary.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r18.anchor: قالوا وكانت حنة قد أمسك عنها الولد حتى أيست فبينا هي تحت شجرة إذ رأت طائرا يزق فرخا له

TABRISI:3:35-36/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36/r19.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:3:35-36/r19.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh reports that God told ʿImrān he would receive a blessed son who would heal the blind and leper, raise the dead by God’s leave, and be a messenger; Ḥanna then vowed her child.
TABRISI:3:35-36/r19.anchor: روي عن أبي عبد الله قال أوحى الله تعالى إلى عمران إني واهب لك ذكرا مباركا

TABRISI:3:35-36#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:35-36#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:35-36#2/r1.claim: Ḥanna asks God to accept her vow with approval; He hears her words and knows her intention, which grounds her confidence.
TABRISI:3:35-36#2/r1.anchor: أي نذري قبول رضا { إنك أنت السميع } لما أقوله

THALABI:v3p52/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p52/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p52/r15.claim: Hanna says she has made the child in her womb devoted to God; a vow is something a person obligates themself to, conditionally or unconditionally.
THALABI:v3p52/r15.anchor: والنذر: ما أوجبه الإنسان على نفسه بشريطة كان ذلك أو بغير شريطة

THALABI:v3p54/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p54/r1.claim: In Mary’s ‘I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast,’ نذرت means ‘I obligated’; the same sense appears when someone vows another’s blood.
THALABI:v3p54/r1.anchor: إني نذرت للرحمن صوما : أي أوجبت

THALABI:v3p54/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p54/r2.claim: The Prophet says that whoever vows obedience to God must fulfill it, while whoever vows disobedience must not fulfill it.
THALABI:v3p54/r2.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من نذر أن يطيع الله فليطعه

THALABI:v3p54/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r3.speaker: الأعشى
THALABI:v3p54/r3.claim: Al-A'sha’s line uses نذرت النذورا as a poetic example of making a vow.
THALABI:v3p54/r3.anchor: قال الأعشى: غشيت لليلي بليل خدورا

THALABI:v3p54/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p54/r4.claim: The idiom نذر فلان دم فلان means that he imposed on himself the duty of killing the person.
THALABI:v3p54/r4.anchor: ومن هذا قولهم: نذر فلان دم فلان: أي أوجبت على نفسه قتله

THALABI:v3p54/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r5.speaker: جميل
THALABI:v3p54/r5.claim: Jamil’s line about men who vowed his blood likewise illustrates the verb نذر.
THALABI:v3p54/r5.anchor: وقال جميل: فليت رجالا فيك قد نذروا دمي

THALABI:v3p54/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p54/r6.claim: محررا means freed, pure, and wholly devoted to God as a servant of the sanctuary, withdrawn from worldly concerns; related usage describes an emancipated slave, a corrected text, an unfettered person, or pure clay.
THALABI:v3p54/r6.anchor: محررا: أي عتيقا خالصا لله خادما للكنيسة حبيسا عليها

THALABI:v3p54/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p54/r7.claim: محررا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.

THALABI:v3p54/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r8.speaker: الكلبي وابن إسحاق وغيرهما
THALABI:v3p54/r8.claim: They describe the Jerusalem sanctuary custom: a consecrated boy served there until puberty, then could choose to stay; if he stayed, he could not leave. Boys alone were assigned because girls were thought unsuitable due to menstruation and impurity.
THALABI:v3p54/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي وابن إسحاق وغيرهما: فإن الحر رجل إذا حرر وجعل في الكنيسة

THALABI:v3p54/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p54/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p54/r9.claim: The narrative says Hanna, childless into old age, saw a bird feeding its young and prayed for a child, vowing to dedicate it to Jerusalem as a caretaker in gratitude; she became pregnant without knowing the child’s sex, worried a girl could not serve, and Imran died while Hanna was pregnant.
THALABI:v3p54/r9.anchor: وكان القصة في ذلك أن زكريا وعمران تزوجا أختين، وكانت إيشاع بنت فاقود أم يحيى عند زكريا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p188/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p188/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p188/r3.claim: A second view connects the verse to the following account: God hears the wife of Imran's words and knows her inward intention when she says her vow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p188/r3.anchor: أن هذه الآية تتصل بما بعدها، تقديرها: {والله سميع} لما تقوله امرأة عمران، {عليم} بما تضمره،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda treats إذ as an idle extra with no grammatical position, so the sense is simply The wife of Imran said.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r1.anchor: فزعم أبو عبيدة (¬3) أنها زائدة، لغو؛ والمعنى: (قالت امرأة عمران)، ولا موضع لها من الإعراب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects Abu Ubayda: a particle that indicates past time cannot be meaningless.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬5): ولم يصنع أبو عبيدة في هذا شيئا، لأن (إذ) تدل على ما مضى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari also rejects dropping the grammatical force of a Qur'anic particle when a meaningful analysis is available.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري (¬6) منكرا لهذا القول أيضا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r4.speaker: الأخفش والمبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash and Al-Mubarrad supply an omitted imperative: Remember when the wife of Imran said.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r4.anchor: قال الأخفش، والمبرد (¬2): المعنى: (اذكر إذ قالت امرأة عمران).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq makes the عامل of إذ the sense of God's choosing the family of Imran: He chose them when the wife of Imran said her vow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق (¬4): المعنى عندي: (واصطفى آل عمران {إذ قالت امرأت عمران})

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r6.claim: Abu Bakr rejects Abu Ishaq's attachment: the choosing of Adam and Noah preceded the wife's statement, and this Imran differs from Imran father of Moses and Aaron by about 1,800 years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r6.anchor: وأنكر أبو بكر هذا، وقال: الله تعالى قرن اصطفاءه [آل عمران] (¬7) باصطفائه آدم ونوحا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r7.claim: Another view links this verse to the preceding description and takes إذ as governed by the sense of Hearing, Knowing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p189#2/r7.anchor: وذكرنا أيضا عن بعض أهل المعاني أن هذه الآية متصلة بما قبلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r1.claim: Imran's wife was Hanne, Mary's mother and Jesus' grandmother; she vowed a child to service in the Jerusalem sanctuary in gratitude, reflecting a custom that children had to fulfill parents' vows of temple service.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r1.anchor: وقوله: {امرأت عمران} هي: حنة (¬4)، أم مريم، جدة عيسى عليه السلام، دعت الله أن يهب لها ولدا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r2.claim: Nadhart means I imposed or obligated; a vow is something a person obligates himself to, conditionally or unconditionally.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r2.anchor: معنى {نذرت}: [أوجبت] (¬1). والنذر: ما يوجبه الإنسان على نفسه بشريطة كان، أو بغير شريطة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r3.claim: Linguists explain a vow as warding off feared harm through a self-imposed good deed; its root is الإنذار, notifying someone of danger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r3.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: معنى النذر: استدفاع المخوف، بما يعقد على النفس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r4.claim: Muḥarraran is a circumstantial accusative modifying ما, understood as the child in her womb in a state of consecration.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r4.anchor: وانتصب {محررا} على الحال من {ما} تقديره: نذرت لك الذي في بطني محررا (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba says she meant to make the child liberated and pure for God, serving the church and worship; muḥarrar denotes anything freed or purified, as in an emancipated slave, refined book, unattached free man, or clean clay.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p191/r5.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة (¬3): أرادت نذرت لك أن أجعل (¬4) ما في بطني محررا، أي: عتيقا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p194/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p194/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p194/r1.claim: Acceptance means taking something with approval; the word derives from meeting or facing because the thing taken is met with recompense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p194/r1.anchor: معنى التقبل (¬1): أخذ الشيء على الرضى (¬2) به (¬3). وأصله، من: المقابلة؛ لأنه يقابل بالجزاء ما يؤخذ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p194/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p194/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p194/r2.claim: God is hearing her supplication and knowing what is in her heart.

QASHANI:3:35-37/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:35-37/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:35-37/r1.claim: God heard the wife of Imran's vow and knew her intention, as she affirmed by calling Him the Hearer and Knower.

QASHANI:3:35-37/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:35-37/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:35-37/r2.claim: Parents' intentions and dispositions affect a child as food affects the body: lawful food, luminous dispositions, and sincere intentions yield a believer, truthful person, saint, or prophet; forbidden food and corrupt dispositions yield a wicked or unbelieving child, since the embryo develops from that food and is nurtured by that soul.
QASHANI:3:35-37/r2.anchor: النيات وهيئات النفس مؤثرة في نفس الولد، كما أن الأغذية مؤثرة في بدنه

QASHANI:3:35-37/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:35-37/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:3:35-37/r3.claim: The Prophet says, The child is the secret of his father; Qashani connects this to Mary's truthfulness and Jesus' blessed filial descent from her truthful father.
QASHANI:3:35-37/r3.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r4.claim: Imran's wife is Hannah, Mary's mother.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r4.anchor: { إذ قالت امرأة عمران } وهي حنة أم مريم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r5.claim: She bound herself to dedicate the child in her womb to God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r5.anchor: { إني نذرت لك ما في بطني } أي: أوجبت على نفسي أن أجعل ما في بطني

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r6.claim: Muharraran means freed, devoted to God, and dedicated to worship and church service; children were obliged to obey such vows, so she gave the child to Jerusalem's temple.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:34-36/r6.anchor: { محررا } عتيقا خالصا لله، خادما للكنيسة، مفرغا للعبادة ولخدمة الكنيسة، وكان على أولادهم فرضا أن يطيعوهم في نذرهم، فتصدقت بولدها على بيت المقدس.

ELMALILI:3:35-37/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r1.claim: In his rendering of the vow, Elmalılı calls Imran’s wife his “harem” and renders the unborn child as dedicated to God “free of every restriction.”
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r1.anchor: İmrân’ın haremi dediği vakit: “Yâ Rabbi! Ben karnımdakini her kayıttan âzâde olarak Sana adadım

ELMALILI:3:35-37/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r2.claim: A report names Jesus’ maternal grandmother, Imran’s wife, as Hanne bint Fakuza; Hanne’s sister—or, in another report, Maryam’s sister—was Iysha, wife of Zakariya and mother of Yahya. The Prophet is reported to call Yahya and Jesus cousins, sons of maternal aunts.
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r2.anchor: Rivayet olunuyor ki Hazret-i Îsâ’nın ninesi zevce-i İmrân’ın ismi “Hanne binti Fâkuza”

ELMALILI:3:35-37/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r3.claim: Muharrar means thoroughly freed or made free; it is explained as a sincere worshipper, a temple servant, or someone freed from worldly concerns.
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r3.anchor: “Muharrer”: Esâsen iyice azadlanmış, hâlis hür yapılmış demektir ki ibadette muhlis veya mabed hâdimi veya dünyadan âzade mânalarıyla tefsir edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r1.claim: The Imran named here and in 66:12 is Mary’s father, hence Jesus’ grandfather; the Qur’an does not name his wife, Mary’s mother.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r1.anchor: Bu âyette ve Tahrîm sûresinin 12. âyetinde anılan İmrân’ın Hz. Meryem’in babası (Hz. Îsâ’nın dedesi) olduğu açıktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r5.claim: Orientalist criticism that alleges a Qur’anic historical contradiction relies on confusion in some Muslim authors; the author calls it non-objective, noting Luke likewise describes Elizabeth as a daughter of Aaron.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r5.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in bu konudaki açıklamalarında herhangi bir çelişki ve tarihî verilerle uyumsuzluk bulunmamaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r6.claim: Islamic sources call Mary’s mother Hanne, while Christian sources call her Anna.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r6.anchor: Onun adı İslâmî kaynaklarda Hanne, hıristiyan kaynaklarda Anna diye geçer.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r7.speaker: bir rivayet
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r7.claim: One report says Imran’s long-childless wife saw a bird feeding its young, prayed for a child, vowed to dedicate it to service at Bayt al-Maqdis, and that Imran died after she became pregnant.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r7.anchor: Bunlardan birine göre, uzun zaman çocuğu olmayan İmrân’ın karısı bir gün bir kuşun yavrusunu beslediğini görünce

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r8.claim: Muharrar literally means someone freed and made entirely independent, with no one retaining a claim over them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r8.anchor: Sözlük anlamı itibariyle muharrar “âzat edilmiş, tamamen özgürlüğüne kavuşturulmuş, kimsenin kendisi üzerinde hak ilintisi kalmamış kişi” demektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r9.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r9.claim: Commentators gloss the vow as freedom from worldly affairs and dedication solely to worship, as a pure servant, or as service to the temple or its scripture readers, reflecting Jewish dedication of children to the sanctuary.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r9.anchor: Burada kelimeye, dünya işlerinden âzâde kılınmış ve kendini sırf Allah’a kulluk etmeye veren; halis bir kul

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r10.claim: Whatever aspect is emphasized, the vow expresses an absolute dedication without conditions; the translation therefore renders muharrar as unconditionally dedicated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:35/r10.anchor: O sebeple meâlinde bu kelimeye “kayıtsız şartsız” anlamı verilmiştir.

BAQILLANI:v1p183/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r1.claim: Detailed criticism of Imruʾ al-Qays’s meter, grammar, and poetry falls outside this book’s purpose, so the author omits it.
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r1.anchor: ثم رأينا هذا خارجا عن غرض كتابنا والكلام فيه يتصل بنقد الشعر

BAQILLANI:v1p183/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r2.claim: Poetry follows an inherited, shared tradition; poets receive and use its resources according to their differing capacities.
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r2.anchor: وإنما أردنا أن نبين الجملة التي بيناها لتعرف أن طريقة الشعر شريعة مورودة

BAQILLANI:v1p183/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r3.claim: Poets may surpass predecessors, overlook meanings predecessors found, or share a meaning; poetic talent is distributed by God.

BAQILLANI:v1p183/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r4.claim: The Qurʾān’s composition and arrangement bewilder minds; the author promises to make its inimitability and supreme eloquence perceptible.
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r4.anchor: فأما نهج القرآن ونظمه وتأليفه ورصفه فإن العقول تتيه في جهته وتحار في بحره

BAQILLANI:v1p183/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r5.claim: The science of Qurʾānic inimitability is noble and difficult, yet has few students and weak advocates.
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r5.anchor: واعلم أن هذا علم شريف المحل عظيم المكان قليل الطلاب ضعيف الأصحاب

BAQILLANI:v1p183/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r6.claim: Even near-synonyms such as “morning” and “dawn” cannot be freely exchanged: one may fit a position where the other sounds misplaced.
BAQILLANI:v1p183/r6.anchor: فإن إحدى اللفظتين قد تنفر في موضع وتزل عن مكان لا تزل عنه اللفظة الأخرى

BAQILLANI:v1p192/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r1.claim: Human discourse may fail in comprehension, completeness, sound construction, wisdom, policy, or leadership; verbal and semantic excellence often come apart.
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r1.anchor: ثم لو ظفرت بذلك كله رأيته ناقصا في وجه الحكمة أو مدخولا في باب السياسة

BAQILLANI:v1p192/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r2.claim: The Qurʾān remains useful when expanded and complete when concise; sustained reflection uncovers successive beauties and inventions.
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r2.anchor: وأنت لا تجد في جميع ما تلونا عليك إلا ما إذا بسط أفاد وإذا اختصر كمل في بابه وجاد

BAQILLANI:v1p192/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r4.claim: The Qurʾān’s inimitable balance holds across short, medium, and long verses; readers should examine openings, endings, transitions, and joins.
BAQILLANI:v1p192/r4.anchor: وهو تعادل هذا النظم في الإعجاز في مواقع الآيات القصيرة والطويلة والمتوسطة

BAQILLANI:v1p196/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p196/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p196/r2.claim: The sequence of divine names and attributes in the opening of Ghāfir gathers noble meanings within an artful opening and close, unmatched in human speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p196/r2.anchor: حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم غافر الذنب

BAQILLANI:v1p196/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p196/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p196/r3.claim: Across the following verses, transitions between argument, threat, excuse, and warning unify varied subjects through elevated composition.
BAQILLANI:v1p196/r3.anchor: ثم اتل ما بعدها من الآي واعرف وجه الخلوص من شيء إلى شيء

BAQILLANI:v1p230/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r1.claim: The line naming Ḥamdawayh al-Aḥwal is ugly, heavy, and inept; the poet’s desire to digress obscures his judgment, though a graceful alternative was possible.
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r1.anchor: ثم قوله حمدوية الأحول وحش جدا فما أمقت هذا البيت وأبغضه

BAQILLANI:v1p230/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r2.claim: The horse-tail verse begins awkwardly and breaks the connection with what precedes; its contrivance fails to sustain the poem’s flow.
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r2.anchor: فالبيت الأول وحش الابتداء منقطع عما سبق من الكلام

BAQILLANI:v1p230/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r3.claim: The phrase should have said “a tail like a robe”; omitting the comparison’s object leaves the connection uneven and inelegant.
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r3.anchor: وكان يحتاج أن يقول ذنب كالرداء فقد حذف والوصل غير متسق

BAQILLANI:v1p230/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r4.claim: “As the robe is dragged” makes an awkward, inaccurate simile unless one supplies the unstated idea that the tail itself is dragged.
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r4.anchor: ثم قوله كما سحب الرداء قبيح في تحقيق التشبيه وليس بواقع

BAQILLANI:v1p230/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r5.claim: The description “defending the rump” is neither apt nor truthful; the author contrasts it with Imruʾ al-Qays’s praised phrase about a tail above the ground.

BAQILLANI:v1p230/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r6.claim: The comparison of the horse’s fetlocks to Orion is attractive but not original; poets commonly compared a horse’s blaze with the moon, stars, and similar images.

BAQILLANI:v1p230/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r7.claim: The omitted twenty lines of horse description can be good or inventive, but remain within the shared practice of poets, among whom others equaled or surpassed him.
BAQILLANI:v1p230/r7.anchor: واعلم أنا تركنا بقية كلامه في وصف الفرس لأنه ذكر عشرين بيتا في ذلك

BURHAN:v2p118/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p118/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p118/r4.claim: Although jawf and baṭn are close in meaning, substituting one for the other in its verse would lose the wording's taste and acceptance.
BURHAN:v2p118/r4.anchor: وكذلك قوله ﴿ ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه ﴾ وفى موضع آخر ﴿ في بطني محررا ﴾ استعمل الجوف فى الأول والبطن فى الثانى

BURHAN:v4p87/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p87/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p87/r1.claim: Definiteness and indefiniteness each suit particular contexts; the author lays out several causes for definiteness.
BURHAN:v4p87/r1.anchor: اعلم إن لكل واحد منهما مقاما لايليق بالآخر فاما التعريف فله اسباب

BURHAN:v4p87/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p87/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p87/r5.claim: The definite male and female identify the particular boy requested and the girl actually born, not men and women in general.

BURHAN:v1p415/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p415/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p415/r7.claim: The open tā in امرأة is used for five wives, marking outward conjugal companionship even though four are inwardly estranged.
BURHAN:v1p415/r7.anchor: كلها ممدودة تنبيها على فعل التبعل الصحبة وشدة المواصلة والمخالطة والائتلاف فى الموجود والمحسوس

BURHAN:v1p415/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p415/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p415/r8.claim: Imran's wife alone remained inwardly and outwardly joined to her husband; God gave her good offspring, honored her, and favored her.
BURHAN:v1p415/r8.anchor: وواحدة خاصة واصلت بعلها باطنا وظاهرا وهى امرأت عمران فجعل الله لها ذرية طيبة

BURHAN:v4p278/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p278/r2.speaker: أبو تمام
BURHAN:v4p278/r2.claim: Abu Tammam's line ويضرب في ذات الإله فيوجع is evidence for the expression ذات.
BURHAN:v4p278/r2.anchor: وعليه قول أبي تمام * ويضرب في ذات الاله فيوجع

SULAMI:v1p98#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r1.claim: Ja'far glosses the vowed child as freed from the bondage of the world and its people.
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r1.anchor: قال جعفر رحمه الله : عتيقا من رق الدنيا وأهلها

SULAMI:v1p98#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن علي
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ali says the child is to be God's sincere servant; whoever is wholly God's is free from everything besides Him.
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن علي رحمه الله في قوله تعالى : ﴿ نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا ﴾ أي : يكون لك عبدا مخلصا

SULAMI:v1p98#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r3.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r3.claim: Sahl defines the liberated person as one freed from personal aims and following caprice.
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r3.anchor: سئل سهل بن عبد الله عن المحرر قال : هو المعتق من إرادات نفسه

SULAMI:v1p98#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r4.speaker: النوري
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r4.claim: Al-Nuri reads the vow as freeing the mother from preoccupation with and management of the child, surrendering the child to God's wise direction.
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r4.anchor: قال النوري - تغمده الله برحمته - في قوله تعالى :

SULAMI:v1p98#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r5.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl says the child is freed from being occupied with earning a livelihood.
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r5.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضل رحمه الله في قوله تعالى :

ITQAN:v4p384/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r20.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r20.claim: Imran’s wife is Hinna daughter of Faqhudh.

ITQAN:v1p87/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p87/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p87/r1.claim: Al-Suyuti describes earlier works on occasions of revelation, including al-Madini’s, al-Wahidi’s deficient work, al-Ja‘bari’s abridgment, and Ibn Hajar’s unfinished manuscript, then presents his concise edited Lubab al-Nuqul.
ITQAN:v1p87/r1.anchor: أفرده بالتصنيف جماعة أقدمهم علي بن المديني شيخ البخاري ومن أشهرها كتاب الواحدي

ITQAN:v1p87/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p87/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p87/r2.claim: Knowledge of an occasion of revelation can show the wisdom behind legislation.
ITQAN:v1p87/r2.anchor: منها معرفة وجه الحكمة الباعثة على تشريع الحكم

ITQAN:v1p87/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p87/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p87/r3.claim: For scholars who hold that the cause governs, the occasion can restrict a ruling to its specific cause.
ITQAN:v1p87/r3.anchor: ومنها تخصيص الحكم به عند من يرى أن العبرة بخصوص السبب

ITQAN:v1p87/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p87/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ITQAN:v1p87/r4.claim: When evidence restricts a general wording, knowing its occasion keeps the restriction from excluding the occasion itself, whose inclusion is certain; al-Qadi Abu Bakr reports consensus against excluding it by independent reasoning.
ITQAN:v1p87/r4.anchor: فإن دخول صورة السبب قطعي وإخراجها بالاجتهاد ممنوع كما حكى الإجماع عليه القاضي أبو بكر

ITQAN:v1p87/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p87/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p87/r5.claim: Knowing the occasion of revelation can clarify a verse’s meaning and remove interpretive difficulty.
ITQAN:v1p87/r5.anchor: ومنها الوقوف على المعنى وإزالة الإشكال

ITQAN:v1p87/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p87/r6.speaker: الواحدي
ITQAN:v1p87/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi says a verse cannot be interpreted without knowing its story and occasion of revelation.
ITQAN:v1p87/r6.anchor: قال الواحدي لا يمكن تفسير الآية دون الوقوف على قصتها وبيان نزولها

ITQAN:v1p87/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p87/r7.speaker: ابن دقيق العيد
ITQAN:v1p87/r7.claim: Ibn Daqiq al-Id calls explaining an occasion of revelation a strong route to understanding Qur’anic meanings.
ITQAN:v1p87/r7.anchor: وقال ابن دقيق العيد بيان سبب النزول طريق قوي في فهم معاني القرآن

ITQAN:v1p87/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p87/r8.speaker: ابن تيمية
ITQAN:v1p87/r8.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says knowing the occasion aids understanding because knowledge of the cause yields knowledge of its effect.
ITQAN:v1p87/r8.anchor: وقال ابن تيمية معرفة سبب النزول يعين على فهم الآية فإن العلم بالسبب يورث العلم بالمسبب

ITQAN:v3p59/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p59/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p59/r1.claim: The proper scope of abrogation is one verse abrogating another; including the final category, which lifts rulings from Islam’s early period, is more apt than the two preceding categories.
ITQAN:v3p59/r1.anchor: حق الناسخ والمنسوخ أن تكون آية نسخت آية

ITQAN:v3p283/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p283/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p283/r6.claim: Abu Shama says supplication can also be classified as declarative, as can all praise; sabbiḥ is imperative, while subḥān may be command, supplication, or declarative.
ITQAN:v3p283/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يذكر مع الخبر وكذا الثناء كله خبر إلا

ITQAN:v3p283/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p283/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p283/r7.claim: A good opening is carefully fashioned because it first strikes the ear: a polished start draws attention and understanding, while a poor one can turn listeners away; it should be graceful, clear, well ordered, and free of confusing complexity.
ITQAN:v3p283/r7.anchor: من البلاغة حسن الابتداء وهو أن يتأنق في أول الكلام لأنه أول ما يقرع السمع

ITQAN:v3p283/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p283/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p283/r8.claim: All sūra openings are excellent and eloquent, whether they begin with praise, disjointed letters, address, or another form.
ITQAN:v3p283/r8.anchor: قالوا وقد أتت جميع فواتح السور على أحسن الوجوه وأبلغها وأكملها كالتحميدات وحروف الهجاء

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r1.speaker: من كان هذا رأيه
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r1.claim: Critics of poetry object to its frivolity, obscenity, lies, meter and rhyme, or the conduct of poets, whom they say revelation condemns.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r1.anchor: لا يخلو من كان هذا رأيه من أمور

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r2.claim: Jurjānī calls these grounds mistaken; condemning poetry for containing vice would require condemning all speech and preferring silence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r2.anchor: فهو في ذلك على خطأ ظاهر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r3.claim: The objection about immoral content fails because prose contains more such material than poetry, since its speakers vastly outnumber poets; one can study only serious poetry.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r4.claim: A transmitter is not blameworthy for quoting unless he intends to support falsehood or harm a Muslim; God quotes unbelievers, and scholars cite indecent lines to explain Qur’anic vocabulary and grammar.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r4.anchor: وقد حكى الله تعالى كلام الكفار

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r5.claim: Scholars cite even obscene poetry to explain rare Qur’anic words and grammar without intending or endorsing its obscenity.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p28/r5.anchor: وقد استشهد العلماء لغريب القرآن وإعرابه بالأبيات فيها الفحش

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r1.claim: A proposition is the root of speech meaning and cannot be conceived without two terms: what is affirmed or denied and that about which it is affirmed or denied.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r1.anchor: معان لا تتصور إلا فيما بين شيئين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r2.claim: A proposition must be formed as verb plus noun or noun plus noun; even a bare adjective such as “ صالح ” implies a subject, as in “هو صالح”.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r2.anchor: أن لا يعقل إلا من مجموع جملة فعل واسم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r3.claim: A proposition also requires an originating speaker, who bears responsibility for its truth or falsehood and is the one affirming or denying.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p383/r3.anchor: لا يتصور أن يكون خبر حتى يكون له مخبر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r1.claim: The phrase about a wounded person complaining to crows and vultures is figurative: do not complain to creatures, as that would be like a sore camel appealing to vultures.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r1.anchor: العبارة الصحيحة في هذا أن يقال : لا تشك إلى خلق فإنك إن فعلت

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r2.claim: One may follow a scholar’s interpretation for a long time, then discover that the matter is contrary to what that scholar judged.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r2.anchor: من ذلك أنك ترى من العلماء من قد تأول في الشيء تأويلا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r3.speaker: الآمدي
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r3.claim: Al-Āmidī treats al-Buḥturī’s weaving and forging by rain as literal, and judges Abū Tammām’s “weaver” wording ugly while approving al-Buḥturī’s wording.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r3.anchor: أبا القاسم الآمدي ذكر بيت البحتري

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r4.claim: Jurjānī rejects al-Āmidī’s reading: in Abū Tammām the seeming “eons” concern how long the weaving appears to take, not whether rain literally weaves.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p399/r4.anchor: فالحيلولة واقعة على كون زمان الحوك حقبا

TUSTARI:3:35/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:35/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:35/r1.claim: Mary's mother freed her child from worldly bondage, following caprice and the ego's desires, and dedicated her to serve the people of the Temple purely for God.
TUSTARI:3:35/r1.anchor: أي حررته وأعتقته من رق الدنيا من متابعة هواه ومرادات نفسه، وجعلته خادما لعباد بيت المقدس

DAMGHANI:v1p431/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r2.claim: The wife of ʿImrān, Maryam's mother, is named Ḥannah.
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r2.anchor: الخامس : امرأة عمران أم مريم وهى حنة . وقوله تعالى فى سورة ال عمران

DAMGHANI:v1p178/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p178/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p178/r11.claim: The entry lists eighteen senses of dhikr: righteous action, speech, inward remembrance, recalling commands or stories, preservation, admonition, honor, report, revelation, Qur'an, Torah, the Preserved Tablet, clarification, reflection, prayers, monotheism, and the Messenger.
DAMGHANI:v1p178/r11.anchor: ذ ك ر على ثمانية عشر وجها العمل الصالح الذكر باللسان الذكر بالقلب الذكر على الأمر والقصة الحفظ العظة الشرف الخبر الوحي القرآن التوراة اللوح المحفوظ البيان التفكر الصلوات الخمس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r6.claim: The wife of ʿImrān is identified as Ḥanna.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r6.anchor: والخامس : حنة . ومنه قوله تعالى في [ آل عمران ] :

FARRA:v1p207/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p207/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p207/r2.claim: Muḥarraran means dedicated to Jerusalem’s sanctuary, with no occupation apart from its service.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p103#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p103#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p103#5/r1.claim: The particle idh can be extra in the wording, as Ibn Qutayba explained in Taʾwīl Mushkil al-Qurʾān.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p103#5/r1.anchor: {إذ قالت امرأت عمران} أي: قالت و"إذ" تزاد في الكلام على ما بينت في "تأويل المشكل" (2) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p103#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p103#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p103#5/r2.claim: Muḥarraran means freed and dedicated to God, withdrawn from worldly service to worship Him and remain in His sanctuary.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p103#5/r2.anchor: {محررا} أي: عتيقا لله عز وجل. تقول: أعتقت الغلام وحررته؛ سواء.

MAJAZ:v1p90/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p90/r1.claim: The phrase is glossed as “the wife of ʿImrān said.”
MAJAZ:v1p90/r1.anchor: «إذ قالت امرأت عمران» (35) معناها: قالت: امرأة عمران

MAJAZ:v1p90/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p90/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p90/r2.claim: Muḥarraran means dedicated and freed for God; aʿtaqtuhu and ḥarrartuhu have the same meaning.
MAJAZ:v1p90/r2.anchor: «محررا» (35) أي عتيقا لله، أعتقته وحررته واحد

NAHHAS:v1p369/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p369/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v1p369/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats idh as extra.
NAHHAS:v1p369/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة إذ زائدة وقال محمد بن يزيد التقدير أذكر إذ قال

NAHHAS:v1p369/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p369/r2.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v1p369/r2.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd supplies an omitted “remember”: remember when the wife of ʿImrān spoke.
NAHHAS:v1p369/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن يزيد التقدير أذكر إذ قال

NAHHAS:v1p369/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p369/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p369/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq connects the clause to God’s choosing of the family of ʿImrān when his wife made her vow.
NAHHAS:v1p369/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق المعنى واصطفى آل عمران إذ قالت امرأة عمران

NAHHAS:v1p369/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p369/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p369/r4.claim: Muḥarraran is best parsed as a circumstantial accusative; the alternative makes it an adjective of an omitted object, a boy dedicated to temple service.
NAHHAS:v1p369/r4.anchor: منصوب على الحال وقيل هو نعت لمفعول محذوف أي نذرت لك ما في بطني غلاما محررا

NAHHAS:v1p369/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p369/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v1p369/r5.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports Ibn ʿAbbās: the aged wife vowed her fetus to service, bore a girl accepted by God; priests cast pens to choose her guardian, and Zakariyyā raised Mary, found out-of-season fruit, and hoped for a son.
NAHHAS:v1p369/r5.anchor: روى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال حملت امرأة عمران بعد ما أسنت فنذرت ما في بطنها محررا

NAHHAS:v1p369/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p369/r6.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v1p369/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says many servants of the scholars became prophets, so only boys were accepted for service.
NAHHAS:v1p369/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك كان أكثر من يجعل خادما للأحبار ينبأ فلذلك كان لا يقبل إلا الغلمان

NAHHAS:v1p369/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p369/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p369/r7.claim: The context favors the circumstantial reading: she says she delivered a female, which was not ordinarily accepted, then God says He accepted her; making the description modify an omitted object also requires an unusual deleted lām.
NAHHAS:v1p369/r7.anchor: قالت رب إني وضعتها أنثى أي وليس الأنثى مما يقبل فقال الله جل وعز فتقبلها ربها

SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r1.claim: One parse supplies an omitted udhkur: idh is then a direct object, not a time adverb; Abū al-Ḥasan and Abū al-ʿAbbās hold this view.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه " اذكر " مقدرا، فيكون مفعولا به لا ظرفا

SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r2.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r2.claim: Another parse supplies an understood iṣṭafā from the earlier verb and attaches idh to it; this makes “the family of ʿImrān” a clause-level coordination, avoiding the impossible claim that Adam's choosing coincided with the wife's speech.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r2.anchor: الثاني: أن الناصب له معنى الاصطفاء أي ب " اصطفى " مقدرا مدلولا عليه باصطفى الأول

SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r3.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r3.claim: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī explicitly makes idh depend on samīʿ; al-Zamakhsharī appears to do likewise, for hearing her speech and intention.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r3.anchor: الثالث: أنه منصوب ب " سميع " وبه صرح ابن جرير الطبري

SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r4.claim: The Shaykh rejects attachment to samīʿ: ʿalīm either interrupts the government or qualifies samīʿ before it takes its object, and divine hearing and knowledge are not time-limited; the author replies that adverbials allow such flexibility.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يصح ذلك لأن قوله " عليم ": إما أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر

SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats idh as redundant; grammarians call this an error, and the author says Abū ʿUbayda was weak in grammar.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35/r5.anchor: الرابع: أن تكون " إذ " زائدة وهو قول أبي عبيدة، والتقدير: قالت امرأة، وهذا عند النحويين غلط

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r1.claim: Muḥarraran may be a circumstantial from the relative phrase mā fī baṭnī, governed by nadhartu.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه حال من الموصول وهو " ما في بطني " ، فالعامل فيها " نذرت "

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is circumstantial from the pronoun governed by the preposition in mā fī baṭnī, with the implicit existential of that phrase as its governor.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنه حال من الضمير المرفوع بالجار لوقوعه صلة ل " ما " ، وهو قريب من الأول

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r3.claim: Muḥarraran can be a verbal noun on the passive-participle pattern: either with an omitted “vow of emancipation” or by sense, since nadhartu laka means “I freed as a freeing.”
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r3.anchor: الثالث: أن ينتصب على المصدر؛ لأن المصدر يأتي على زنة اسم المفعول من الفعل الزائد

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r4.claim: The pattern is illustrated by Qurʾān 34:19 and 22:18 and a poet's masraḥ al-qawāfī, meaning tasrīḥ al-qawāfī.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r4.anchor: ومن مجيء المصدر بزنة المفعول مما زاد على الثلاثي قوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r5.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r5.claim: Makkī makes muḥarraran an adjective of a deleted object, “a freed boy”; Ibn ʿAṭiyya questions this because nadhara already has mā fī baṭnī as its object.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r5.anchor: الرابع: أن يكون نعت مفعول محذوف تقديره: غلاما محررا، قاله مكي بن أبي طالب

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r6.claim: If muḥarraran is circumstantial, it is contemporaneous when it means emancipation, but prospective when it means service in a church, as reported in tafsīr.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r6.anchor: وعلى القول بأنها حال يجوز أن تكون حالا مقارنة إن أريد بالتحرير معنى العتق

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī pause on imraʾah with hāʾ despite the written tāʾ; Medinans pause with tāʾ following the muṣḥaf spelling, an Arabic dialect also heard in ḥamzat and witnessed by a poet's Muslimat.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r7.anchor: ووقف أبو عمرو والكسائي على " امرأة " بالهاء دون التاء، وقد كتبوا امرأة بالتاء

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r8.speaker: أهل المدينة
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r8.claim: The people of Medina pause with tāʾ according to the written muṣḥaf; comparable pause forms occur in “the wife of al-ʿAzīz,” Noah's and Lot's wives, and Pharaoh's wife.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#2/r8.anchor: وأهل المدينة يقفون بالتاء اتباعا لرسم المصحف، وهي لغة للعرب

SAMIN-DURR:3:35#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#3/r1.claim: Mā is used instead of man because the contents of the womb are still unknown; those restricting mā to nonrational referents explain it by that ambiguity or the fetus's lack of discernment, while those allowing rational referents need no special explanation.
SAMIN-DURR:3:35#3/r1.anchor: وقوله: { ما في بطني } أتى ب " ما " التي لغير العاقل لأن ما فيه بطنها مبهم أمره

SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.claim: Sībawayh requires عولة لك to follow ويلة لك, and عول لك to follow ويل لك; one expression follows the other, as ينوءك follows يسوءك.
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.anchor: ولا تقول عولة لك إلا أن يكون قبلها ويلة لك ولا تقول عول لك حتى تقول

SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.claim: Some Arabs use ويلا له, ويلة له, and عولة لك as exclamations in the sense of خيبة; Jarir supplies poetic evidence for ويل.
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.anchor: واعلم أن بعض العرب يقول ويلا له وويلة له وعولة لك ويجريها

SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.claim: In response to يا ويلاه, speakers say ويلا كيلا, glossed as making the invoked woe apply to the caller; the reply also means that this is the caller's lot.
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.anchor: ويقول الرجل يا ويلاه فيقول الآخر ويلا كيلا كأنه لك ما دعوت به

SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.claim: A variant يا ويلا كيلا is also used, on the pattern of curses such as جدعا وعقرا.
SIBAWAYH:ولاتقولعولةلكإلاأنيكونقبلهاويلة.anchor: ويلا كيلا وإن شاء جعله على قوله جدعا وعقرا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.claim: The lām of attribution conveys ownership or entitlement, as in الغلام لك and العبد لك; Sībawayh relates it to possessive constructions.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.anchor: ولام الإضافة ومعناها الملك واستحقاق الشيء ألا ترى أنك تقول الغلام لك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.claim: إن is emphatic; when lightened it retains emphasis.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.anchor: لقوله زيد منطلق وإذا خففت فهي كذلك تؤكد ما يتكلم به

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.claim: When إن is lightened, emphatic lām is required as compensation for what was omitted.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعدةمايكونعليهالكلم)#747/.anchor: لام التوكيد تلزمها عوضا مما ذهب منها

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats idh as redundant here and in the angels' statement, effectively meaning simply “she said.”
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معناه قالت امرأة عمران

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r2.speaker: النحويون
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r2.claim: The grammarians say idh is a noun signaling past time, so it cannot be meaningless.
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r2.anchor: قال جميع النحويين: إن (إذ) يدل على ما مضى من الوقت فكيف يكون الدليل على ما مضى من الوقت لغوا

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش وأبو العباس محمد بن يزيد
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad supply an implied imperative: remember when the wife of ʿImrān said.
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r3.anchor: أبو الحسن الأخفش، وأبو العباس محمد بن يزيد: المعنى اذكروا إذ قالت امرأة عمران.

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r4.claim: He makes idh depend on the sense of God's choosing: He chose ʿImrān's family when his wife made the vow.

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r6.claim: The vow dedicates the unborn child as a servant in the sanctuary; children were obliged to obey their parents' vow.
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r6.anchor: أي: جعلته خادما يخدم في متعبداتنا، وكان ذلك جائزا لهم، وكان على أولادهم فرضا أن يطيعوهم في نذرهم،

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r7.claim: The custom concerned male children serving in worship; women were not eligible, so Mary seemed unsuitable when born a girl.
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r7.anchor: ولم يكن ذلك النذر في النساء إنما كان ذلك في الذكورة، فلما ولدت امرأة عمران مريم قالت: (رب إني وضعتها أنثى)

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.claim: Triliteral verbs expanded to quadriliteral patterns take matching verbal-noun patterns, as with jalbaba/jalbaba and shamlala/shamlala.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.anchor: على ذلك أن المصدر كالمصدر من بنات الأربعة نحو جلببت جلببة وشمللت شمللة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.claim: These expanded forms may also take initial tāʾ to form derivatives such as taqallasā and tashayṭana, with corresponding verbal nouns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.anchor: التاء في أوائلها كما لحقت في تدحرج وذلك قولك قلسيته فتقلسى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.claim: Inserted nūn occurs only with specified augmented triliterals, including forms whose extra element is at the lām position or final yāʾ; their inflection follows istifʿala.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.anchor: ولم تزد هذه النون في هذه الأشياء إلا فيما كانت الزيادة فيه من

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.claim: Sībawayh treats the listed augmented triliteral patterns as the full inventory; anything beyond them is not Arabic usage, and he gives their verbal nouns and distributions.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.anchor: ما جاوز هذه الأمثلة فليس من كلام العرب وبينت مصادرهن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.claim: Hamza, yāʾ, tāʾ, and nūn uniquely prefix verbs, including unaugmented and augmented forms, when the action is non-past.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.anchor: وذلك قولك أفعل ويفعل ونفعل وتفعل وقد بين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.claim: Some augment positions are shared across noun and verb patterns while others are not: yāʾ occurs in the cited fourth-position forms where wāw, tāʾ, and mīm do not.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.anchor: وتقول أفعل نحو أفكل فالياء تلحق رابعة والواو لا تلحق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.claim: To identify shared augment positions, compare the number of letters and the position of the added element; unshared forms are recognized by departing from that position.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنبناتالثل.anchor: الذي عنيت في الشركة فتفطن له فإنه يتبين في الفصول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r1.claim: Bint al-Shati says the earlier scholar argued like a theologian rather than a rhetorician, yet defended Qur'anic inimitability through eloquence and defined nazm as familiar Arabic forms raised to an unsurpassable eloquent rank.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r1.anchor: وفي كل ذلك، كان يجادل على طريقة الكلاميين لا البلاغيين. وحسبنا على كل حال، أنه أكد نصره لوجه إعجاز القرآن بفصاحته

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r2.claim: She judges al-Baqillani's book closer to theological and sectarian polemic and literary criticism of long poetic and prose texts than to a dedicated Qur'anic study of inimitability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r2.anchor: وليس دراسة قرآنية خالصة للإعجاز كما يُفهم من عنوانه وكما تَعدِ مقدمتُه، بل هي أقرب إلى الجدل الكلامي والمذهبي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r3.claim: Al-Baqillani's opening chapters refute positions on inimitability rejected by the Ash'aris, the claim that God's oneness cannot be known through the Qur'an, and Zoroastrian claims that their books are miraculous.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r3.anchor: في الفصول الأولى، يتصدى الباقلاني لتخطئة أقوال في الإعجاز، رفضها الأشاعرة وهو منهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r4.claim: She says al-Baqillani presents opponents' objections without naming them and attacks and disparages them sharply.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r4.anchor: وهو في هذا كله يورد شبهات الخصوم دون ذكر أسمائهم، ويشتد في تجريحهم والطعن عليهم والزراية بهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r5.claim: Al-Baqillani briefly passes over foretelling the future and past events since Adam, then centers the third Ash'ari account: the Qur'an's singular arrangement and consummate eloquence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r5.anchor: بعد ذلك ينقل عن الأشاعرة ثلاثة أوجه في الإعجاز، فلا يطيل الوقوف عند الأول والثاني منها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r6.claim: Although the book seems to turn to rhetorical analysis, al-Baqillani repeatedly returns to exhausting theological disputation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r6.anchor: فتحسبه قد تجرد للدرس البلاغي لبديع نظم القرآن، لكنه لا يلبث أن يستطرد بين حين وآخر إلى جدل كلامي مُجهِد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r7.speaker: author
