BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r7.claim: In his rhetoric chapters, al-Baqillani does not examine Qur'anic eloquence closely; he reproduces long poems and speeches and hastily criticizes them to forestall claims that poetry could rival the Qur'an.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p110/r7.anchor: بل إنه فيكا يختص بالفصول البلاغية التي عقدها، لا يفرغ للنظر في أسرار البيان القرآني

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r1.claim: The Qur’anic expression is uniquely elevated and sublime; its eloquence astonished the Arabs, who could not produce anything comparable.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r1.anchor: لا خلاف بين أهل العلم أن التعبير القرآني تعبير فريد في عُلُوِّهِ وسُمُوِّهِ

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r2.claim: The challenge escalated from ten fabricated surahs to one surah, then declared that all humans and jinn together could never match the Qur’an.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r2.anchor: تحداهم أولاً بأن يأتوا بعشر سور مثله إن كانوا يرون أنه مفترى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r3.claim: The one-surah challenge includes short as well as long surahs; Arabs knew they could not answer it and found war and coalition-building easier.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r3.anchor: ويشمل هذا التحدي قِصارَ السور كما يشمل طوالها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r4.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquence so affected hearers that opponents tried to stop people listening, since merely hearing it shook the soul powerfully.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r4.anchor: مجرد وصوله إلى السمع يُحْدِثُ في النفس دَويّاً هائلاً وهِزَّة عنيفة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r5.claim: Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, and al-Akhnas secretly listened to the Prophet recite for three nights, then repeatedly vowed not to return.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r5.anchor: أبي جهل وأبي سفيان والأخنس بن شريق

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r6.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r6.claim: After rejecting labels such as poet, soothsayer, sorcerer, and madman, al-Walid praised the Qur’an’s sweetness, beauty, and superiority.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r6.anchor: قول الوليد بن المغيرة بِسِرٍّ. فقد اجتمع إليه نفر من قريش

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r7.claim: Qur’anic expression is deliberate at the level of every word and letter; placement considers the whole Qur’an, not only an individual verse or surah.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r7.anchor: كل لفظة بل كل حرف فيه وُضِعَ وضعاً فنياً مقصوداً

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r8.speaker: ملاك التأويل
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r8.claim: Early scholars observed that disconnected-letter surahs often repeat their opening letter in their words; the book argues this by comparing similarly sized surahs.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r8.anchor: إن هذه السور إنما وقع في أول كل سورة منها ما كثر تَردادهُ فيما تركب من كَلِمها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r9.speaker: ملاك التأويل
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r9.claim: As a statistical example, Yunus contains about 220 words built on rāʾ, while the nearest non-initial-letter comparator, al-Nahl, has about 200 despite being longer.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r9.anchor: تكرر في سورة يونس من الكلام الواقع فيها الراء مائتا كلمة وعشرون كلمة أو نحوها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r10.claim: The fourteen disconnected letters are half the alphabet and occur across 29 surahs; together they include half of numerous phonetic letter classes.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r10.anchor: أن عدد هذه الحروف أربعة عشر حرفاً أي بمقدار نصف حروف المعجم ترددت في تسع وعشرين سورة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r11.claim: The author cites word-count symmetry: al-dunya and al-ākhirah each occur 115 times, angels and devils 88, and death and life (with derivatives) 145.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r11.anchor: أن (الدنيا) تكررت في القرآن بقدر (الآخرة) فقد تكرر كُلُّ منهما 115 مرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r12.claim: Further counts pair summer and heat with winter and cold five times, and bad deeds with good deeds (including derivatives) 167 times.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r12.anchor: وأن (الصيف) والحر تكررا قدر لفظ (الشتاء) والبرد فقد تكرر كل منهما خمس مرات

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r13.claim: The author also pairs kufr with īmān 17 times, kufran with īmānan eight times, and Iblis with the term for seeking refuge 11 times.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r13.anchor: وأن لفظ (الكفر) تكرر بقدر لفظ (الإيمان) فقد تكرر كل منهما 17 مرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r14.claim: Other asserted count matches pair al-kāfirūn with fire and war with captives; qālū and the command qul each occur 332 times.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r15.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r15.claim: The singular word for month occurs 12 times, singular day 365 times, and plural days 30 times, corresponding to calendar counts.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r15.anchor: وأن لفظ (الشهر) تكرر 12 مرة بعدد الشهور السنة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r16.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r16.claim: He explains the singular/plural count pattern through Arabic usage: plural forms mark paucity (three to ten), while singular forms can mark large quantities.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r16.anchor: تستعمل الجمع تمييزا لأقل العدد وهو ثلاثة إلى عشرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r17.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r17.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r17.claim: He extends the rule to adjectives: a plural adjective suggests fewer described objects, while a singular adjective suggests many.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r17.anchor: فالوصف بالمفرد يدل على الكثرة، والوصف بالجمع يدل على القلة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r18.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r18.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r18.claim: Singular verb agreement can indicate many spears and feminine plural agreement few; he illustrates the pattern in 9:36 with منها for twelve months and فيهن for four sacred months.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r19.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r19.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r19.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that the Qur’an’s wonders never run out and it does not grow stale through repeated recitation.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r19.anchor: لا تنقضي عجائبه ولا يَخلَقُ من كثرة الرد

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r20.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r20.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r20.claim: The author says the Qur’an uses plural الرياح for winds bringing good and mercy, but singular الريح for evil and punishment.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2/r20.anchor: استعمل (الرياح) حيث وردت في القرآن الكريم في الخير والرحمة، واستعمل (الريح) في الشر والعقوبات

NASHR:v1p134/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p134/r1.claim: Abu Amr was born in 68 or 70 AH and died in 154 according to most reports, with other dates also transmitted; the author praises his Qur'an and Arabic learning, integrity, and piety.
NASHR:v1p134/r1.anchor: (وتوفي) أبو عمرو في قول الأكثرين سنة أربع وخمسين ومائة، وقيل: سنة خمس

NASHR:v1p134/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r2.speaker: الحسن
NASHR:v1p134/r2.claim: Hasan, seeing Abu Amr's crowded study circle, said scholars nearly became lords and that honor without knowledge ends in humiliation.
NASHR:v1p134/r2.anchor: مر الحسن به وحلقته متوافرة والناس عكوف عليه، فقال: لا إله إلا الله، لقد كاد العلماء أن يكونوا أربابا

NASHR:v1p134/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
NASHR:v1p134/r3.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna reported a dream in which the Prophet directed him to recite according to Abu Amr when readings differed.
NASHR:v1p134/r3.anchor: وروينا عن سفيان بن عيينة قال: رأيت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في المنام فقلت

NASHR:v1p134/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p134/r4.claim: Al-Yazidi died in 202 AH at age 74, or according to another report after 90; he was a trusted, eloquent authority in languages and literature who memorably dictated ten thousand pages from memory on Abu Amr alone.
NASHR:v1p134/r4.anchor: (وتوفي) اليزيدي سنة اثنتين ومائتين عن أربع وسبعين سنة، وقيل: جاوز التسعين

NASHR:v1p134/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p134/r5.claim: Al-Duri died in 246 AH and was the leading, precise recitation authority of his era; the author says he was the first to collect the readings and that the ten readings were transmitted through him.
NASHR:v1p134/r5.anchor: وكان إمام القراءة في عصره، وشيخ الإقراء في وقته ثقة ثبتا ضابطا كبيرا، وهو أول من جمع القراءات

NASHR:v1p134/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p134/r6.claim: Al-Susi died in 261 AH near age 90 and was a reliable, exact reciter and among al-Yazidi's foremost and eldest students.
NASHR:v1p134/r6.anchor: (وتوفي) السوسي أول سنة إحدى وستين ومائتين، وقد قارب التسعين، وكان مقرئا ضابطا

NASHR:v1p134/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r7.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p134/r7.claim: Abu al-Zar'a was a trusted, exacting authority; al-Dani calls him one of al-Duri's greatest, most distinguished, and most reliable students.
NASHR:v1p134/r7.anchor: قال الداني هو من أكبر أصحاب الدوري وأجلهم وأوثقهم

NASHR:v1p134/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p134/r8.claim: Ibn Farah, known as al-Mufassir because of his knowledge of tafsir, read all of al-Duri's readings from him and was regarded as reliable, distinguished, and exact.
NASHR:v1p134/r8.anchor: قرأ على الدوري بجميع ما قرأ به من القراءات، وكان عالما بالتفسير

NASHR:v1p134/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p134/r9.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p134/r9.claim: Al-Muaddil was a trusted, precise recitation leader whose local peers did not contest his leadership, according to al-Dani.
NASHR:v1p134/r9.anchor: قال الداني: انفرد بالإمامة في عصره ببلده فلم ينازعه في ذلك أحد من أقرانه

NASHR:v1p166/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p166/r1.claim: Hamza died in 156 AH and was a leading, trusted Kufan reciter after Asim and al-Amash, learned in Qur'an, Arabic, and legal inheritance, and known for worship and asceticism.
NASHR:v1p166/r1.anchor: وكان إمام الناس في القراءة بالكوفة بعد عاصم والأعمش، وكان ثقة كبيرا حجة رضيا قيما بكتاب الله

NASHR:v1p166/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
NASHR:v1p166/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa told Hamza that the two fields in which Hamza had surpassed them were Qur'an recitation and inheritance law.
NASHR:v1p166/r2.anchor: شيئان غلبتنا عليهما لسنا ننازعك عليهما: القرآن، والفرائض

NASHR:v1p166/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r3.speaker: الأعمش
NASHR:v1p166/r3.claim: Al-Amash called Hamza a master of the Qur'an; Hamza himself said he had read no Qur'anic letter without transmitted evidence.
NASHR:v1p166/r3.anchor: وكان شيخه الأعمش إذا رآه يقول: هذا حبر القرآن. وقال حمزة: ما قرأت حرفا من كتاب الله إلا بأثر

NASHR:v1p166/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p166/r4.claim: Khalaf died in 229 AH; the author postpones his fuller biography to the account of his own reading.

NASHR:v1p166/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r5.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p166/r5.claim: Khallad died in 220 AH and was an exact, accomplished recitation imam; al-Dani calls him the most precise and distinguished of Sulaym's students.
NASHR:v1p166/r5.anchor: قال الداني: هو أضبط أصحاب سليم وأجلهم

NASHR:v1p166/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p166/r6.claim: Sulaym, Hamza's closest and most exact student, succeeded him in teaching recitation; he died in 187 or 188 AH.
NASHR:v1p166/r6.anchor: وكان أخص أصحاب حمزة وأضبطهم وأقومهم لحروف حمزة، وهو الذي خلفه في القيام بالقراءة

NASHR:v1p166/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r7.speaker: يحيى بن عبد الملك
NASHR:v1p166/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Abd al-Malik recalled that students were told to be especially careful whenever Sulaym arrived to teach.
NASHR:v1p166/r7.anchor: قال يحيى بن عبد الملك: كنا نقرأ على حمزة، فإذا جاء سليم قال لنا تحفظوا

NASHR:v1p166/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r8.speaker: الدارقطني
NASHR:v1p166/r8.claim: Idris, who transmitted Khalaf's narration and selection, was an exact and trusted imam; al-Daraqutni judged him trustworthy and beyond ordinary trustworthiness.
NASHR:v1p166/r8.anchor: وسئل عنه الدارقطني فقال: ثقة وفوق الثقة بدرجة

NASHR:v1p166/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p166/r9.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p166/r9.claim: Ibn Miqsam was an imam in both readings and grammar, known for precision, Arabic, lexicon, and strong writing on Qur'anic disciplines, according to al-Dani.
NASHR:v1p166/r9.anchor: قال الداني: مشهور بالضبط والإتقان عالم بالعربية حافظ للغة، حسن التصنيف في علوم القرآن

NASHR:v1p217/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p217/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p217/r1.claim: The letter ta must retain its strong, closed articulation so it does not become lax or turn into sīn; this matters especially when it is still or repeated, as in the cited examples.
NASHR:v1p217/r1.anchor: التاء: يتحفظ بما فيها من الشدة لئلا تصير رخوة كما ينطق بها بعض الناس، وربما جعلت سينا

NASHR:v1p217/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p217/r2.speaker: سيبويه
NASHR:v1p217/r2.claim: Sibawayh classed ta among the qalqala letters; repeated consonants need particular care because articulation is difficult, which is why Abu Amr and others assimilate them when conditions permit.
NASHR:v1p217/r2.anchor: ولذا أدخلها سيبويه في جملة حروف القلقلة، وليكن التحفظ بها إذا تكررت آكد

NASHR:v1p217/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p217/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p217/r3.claim: Repeated like consonants are hard to articulate clearly; Abu Amr and others therefore favor assimilation when its conditions are met, while emphatic neighbors require especially clear, softened articulation.
NASHR:v1p217/r3.anchor: لصعوبة اللفظ بالمكرر على اللسان، قالوا: هو بمنزلة من في القيد

NASHR:v1p217/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p217/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p217/r4.claim: Because thā is a weak letter, preserve it when quiescent, especially next to a similar or emphatic letter; many non-Arabs instead pronounce it as pure sīn.
NASHR:v1p217/r4.anchor: والثاء حرف ضعيف، فإذا وقع ساكنها فليحتفظ في بيانه، لا سيما إذا أتى بعده حرف يقاربه

NASHR:v1p217/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p217/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p217/r5.claim: The jīm should come from its proper articulation; otherwise it may blend with shīn, as some Syrians and Egyptians pronounce it, or with kāf.
NASHR:v1p217/r5.anchor: والجيم يجب أن يتحفظ بإخراجها من مخرجها فربما خرجت من دون مخرجها

NASHR:v2p129#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p129#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p129#2/r1.claim: The chapter treats substitution of one letter for another, including feminine hāʾ written as tāʾ; those forms divide into readings agreed as singular and forms on which readers differ.
NASHR:v2p129#2/r1.anchor: فهو إبدال حرف بآخر، وهو من المختلف فيه ينحصر في أصل مطرد، وكلمات مخصوصة

NASHR:v2p129#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p129#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p129#2/r2.claim: The agreed singular-reading group includes written forms such as رحمت، نعمت، امرأت، سنت، لعنت، and معصيت الرسول, with the listed repetitions and seven other forms.
NASHR:v2p129#2/r2.anchor: القسم المتفق على إفراده جملته في القرآن أربع عشرة كلمة تكرر منها ستة

NASHR:v2p129#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p129#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p129#2/r3.claim: For the seven nonrepeated forms, including the listed words such as كلمة، بقية، قرة، فطرة، شجرة، جنة, and ابنة, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, al-Kisa'i, and Yaqub stop with hāʾ; Ibn al-Jazari adopts this from the transmitted texts and their analogical implication.
NASHR:v2p129#2/r3.anchor: فوقف على هذه المواضع بالهاء خلافا للرسم ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب، هذا هو الذي قرأنا به ونأخذ به

NASHR:v2p129#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p129#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p129#2/r4.claim: Silence by earlier manuals does not establish that no reading exists; Ibn al-Jazari cites differing manuals and says a transmitter who preserved a reading outweighs one who omitted it.
NASHR:v2p129#2/r4.anchor: فإن من حفظ حجة على من لم يحفظ وغاية من لم يذكر ذلك السكوت، ولا حجة فيه

NASHR:v1p488/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p488/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p488/r1.claim: Of the proposed pause combinations for قل أأنبيكم, only the ten previously set out are valid; nine involving a final yā-like easing, pure wāw substitution for the second hamza, and naql on the first with a fully realized second are rejected.
NASHR:v1p488/r1.anchor: لا يصح منها سوى العشرة المتقدمة، فإن التسعة التي مع تسهيل الأخيرة كالياء، وهو الوجه المعضل، لا يصح

NASHR:v1p488/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p488/r2.speaker: أبو شامة
NASHR:v1p488/r2.claim: Abu Shama reports three positions from Ibn Mihran: ease all three hamzas by transmission and make the latter two between, ease only the third, or ease the last two while disregarding the initial hamza.
NASHR:v1p488/r2.anchor: قال أبو شامة: نص ابن مهران فيها على ثلاثة أوجه: أحدها أن يخفف الثلاثة الأولى بالنقل

NASHR:v1p488/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p488/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p488/r3.claim: A hypothetical fourth approach easing the first and last but not the middle hamza fails, since easing the initial one entails easing the medial one even more strongly.
NASHR:v1p488/r3.anchor: وكان يحتمل وجها رابعا، وهو تخفيف الأولى والأخيرة دون الثانية لولا أن من خفف الأولى يلزمه أن يخفف الثانية

NASHR:v1p488/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p488/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p488/r4.claim: For قل أأنتم, the valid options include stopping on the lām with either facilitation or realization of the second hamza, and no stop with facilitation; realization without the stop and other cited combinations are invalid or doubtful.
NASHR:v1p488/r4.anchor: أحدها السكت على اللام مع تسهيل الهمزة الثانية

NASHR:v1p488/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p488/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p488/r5.claim: For قالوا آمنا after a consonant, the first option—realizing the hamza without sakt—is the majority position; a second option with sakt is attributed to Abu al-Shadha'i and also cited by al-Hudhali.
NASHR:v1p488/r5.anchor: أحدها التحقيق مع عدم السكت، وهو مذهب الجمهور (والثاني) مع السكت، وهو مذهب أبي الشذائي

NASHR:v2p167/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p167/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p167/r1.claim: Across the listed yāʾ of attachment before a kasra hamza, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Abu Ja'far generally open the yāʾ while the other readers make it quiescent, subject to the enumerated exceptions.
NASHR:v2p167/r1.anchor: ففتحها نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وأسكنها الباقون إلا أنهم اختلفوا

NASHR:v2p167/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p167/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p167/r2.claim: Nafi and Abu Ja'far alone open eight listed yāʾs: the two أنصاري إلى الله occurrences, بعبادي إنكم, three ستجدني إن occurrences, بناتي إن, and لعنتي إلى; Ibn Amir joins them for رسلي إن.
NASHR:v2p167/r2.anchor: فتح نافع وأبو جعفر وحدهما ثماني ياءات وهن أنصاري إلى في الموضعين في آل عمران والصف

NASHR:v2p167/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p167/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p167/r3.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, Abu Ja'far, and Hafs open eleven yāʾs: أجري in nine locations plus يدي إليك and أمي إلهين; Ibn Amir agrees on وأمي and أجري.
NASHR:v2p167/r3.anchor: واتفق نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وحفص على فتح إحدى عشرة ياء، وهي أجري في المواضع التسعة

NASHR:v2p167/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p167/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p167/r4.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far, and Ibn Amir open آبائي إبراهيم in Yusuf and دعائي إلا in Noah.
NASHR:v2p167/r4.anchor: واتفق نافع وابن كثير وأبو جعفر وابن عامر على فتح ياءين، وهما آبائي إبراهيم في يوسف ودعائي إلا في نوح

NASHR:v2p167/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p167/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p167/r5.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Abu Ja'far open توفيقي إلا in Hud and حزني إلى الله in Yusuf.
NASHR:v2p167/r5.anchor: واتفق نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو جعفر على فتح توفيقي إلا في هود وحزني إلى الله في يوسف

NASHR:v2p167/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p167/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p167/r6.claim: Abu Ja'far and al-Azraq from Warsh open إخوتي إن in Yusuf; al-Attar alone also reports it through specified routes from al-Asbahani for Warsh and al-Hulwani for Qalun, against the other transmitters on those routes.
NASHR:v2p167/r6.anchor: واختص أبو جعفر والأزرق عن ورش، بفتح ياء واحدة، وهي إخوتي إن في يوسف، وانفرد أبو علي العطار

NASHR:v2p246#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p246#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p246#2/r1.claim: The author's authorities affirm stopping on نذهبن with an alif; although several major readers' manuals are silent, Ibn al-Jazari says the explicit attestation settles the matter in favor of alif.
NASHR:v2p246#2/r1.anchor: وقد ثبت النص بالألف - والله أعلم -

NASHR:v2p246#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p246#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p246#2/r2.claim: Abu Ja'far doubles the nūn in لكن الذين اتقوا here and in al-Zumar, while the other readers leave it light in both places.
NASHR:v2p246#2/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد النون فيهما، وقرأ الباقون بالتخفيف فيهما

NASHR:v2p246#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p246#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p246#2/r3.claim: For وجهي لله, the two Medinan readers, Ibn Amir, and Hafs open the yāʾ; for مني إنك and لي آية, the two Medinans and Abu Amr open it.
NASHR:v2p246#2/r3.anchor: فتحها المدنيان، وابن عامر وحفص (مني إنك) و (لي آية) فتحها المدنيان وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v2p246#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p246#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p246#2/r4.claim: The two Medinan readers open إني أعيذها and أنصاري إلى الله; for إني أخلق, the two Medinans, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr open the yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p246#2/r4.anchor: فتحها المدنيان (إني أخلق) فتحها المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v2p246#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p246#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p246#2/r5.claim: For ومن اتبعن, the two Medinans and Abu Amr retain the yāʾ in connection, while Yaqub retains it in both states; a report also attributes both-state retention to Ibn Shanabudh from Qunbul.
NASHR:v2p246#2/r5.anchor: ومن اتبعن أثبتها في الوصل المدنيان، وأبو عمرو وأثبتها في الحالتين يعقوب

NASHR:v2p246#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p246#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p246#2/r6.claim: Yaqub retains the yāʾ of وأطيعون in both connected and stopped reading.

NASHR:v2p246#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p246#2/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p246#2/r7.claim: For وخافون, Abu Ja'far, Abu Amr, and Ismail retain the yāʾ in connection; Ibn Shanabudh from Qunbul is also reported to do so.
NASHR:v2p246#2/r7.anchor: وخافون أثبتها في الوصل أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وإسماعيل

NASHR:v2p179#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p179#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p179#2/r1.claim: The first class of extra yāʾs is the deleted ending of vocative nouns; readers agree to omit it both in connection and pause, except Ruways at يا عباد فاتقون.
NASHR:v2p179#2/r1.anchor: وهذا القسم مما لا خلاف في حذف الياء منه في الحالين

NASHR:v2p179#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p179#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p179#2/r2.claim: Only يا عبادي الذين آمنوا in al-Ankabut and at the end of al-Zumar are written with this yāʾ without disagreement; يا عباد لا خوف عليكم in al-Zukhruf is disputed.
NASHR:v2p179#2/r2.anchor: ولم يثبت في المصاحف من ذلك سوى موضعين، بلا خلاف وهما ياعبادي الذين آمنوا في العنكبوت

NASHR:v2p179#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p179#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p179#2/r3.claim: The second class occurs at the ends of nouns and verbs, where yāʾ may be a root consonant or a first-person possessive suffix; that is the class treated in this chapter.
NASHR:v2p179#2/r3.anchor: تقع الياء فيه في الأسماء والأفعال نحو الداعي، والجواري، والمنادي

NASHR:v2p179#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p179#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p179#2/r4.claim: This class is defined by deletion in the written muṣḥaf and disagreement over retaining or deleting the yāʾ in connection or both connection and pause; when retained it is followed by a vowel.
NASHR:v2p179#2/r4.anchor: وضابطه أن تكون الياء محذوفة رسما مختلفا في إثباتها وحذفها وصلا، أو وصلا ووقفا

NASHR:v2p179#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p179#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p179#2/r5.claim: The interior-of-verse class contains 35 yāʾs: 13 are original root letters and 22 are additional first-person yāʾs; the author illustrates the original group with several words.
NASHR:v2p179#2/r5.anchor: فهو خمس وثلاثون ياء منها ما الياء فيه أصلية، وهي ثلاث عشرة ياء وباقيها، وهو اثنان وعشرون ياء

NASHR:v2p63#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p63#2/r5.claim: Ibn Dhakwan differs in reports on imāla for عمران, الإكرام, and إكراههن; the Tajrid records only imāla, through al-Akhfash and several transmitters.
NASHR:v2p63#2/r5.anchor: وأما عمران، وهو في قوله آل عمران، وامرأة عمران، ابنت عمران والإكرام وهو الموضعان في سورة الرحمن، إكراههن

QIRAAT-ER:3:35:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:35:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:35:15#1/r1.claim: The standard reading uses the first person yāʾ in its basic form.
QIRAAT-ER:3:35:15#1/r1.anchor: Standard reading with yāʾ al-mutakallim in its basic form

QIRAAT-ER:3:35:15#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:35:15#2/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:3:35:15#2/r1.claim: The variant places fatḥa on the final yāʾ, changing pronunciation and melody but not meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:3:35:15#2/r1.anchor: Variant with fatḥa on the final yāʾ (minniya) — a phonological variant in the treatment of the 1st person pronoun suffix

IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r1.claim: Mary's mother made the unborn child free and devoted to God's worship, with no worldly use intended.
IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r1.anchor: أي نذرته فجعلته عتيقا، تعبده لله، لا ينتفع به لشيء من الدنيا

IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r2.claim: The male is not like the female in this vow, since the child was being dedicated to God as an offering.
IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r2.anchor: أي ليس الذكر كالأنثى لما جعلتها محررا لك [4] نذيرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r1.claim: Muḥarrar is the passive participle of ḥarrara; taḥrīr means emancipation, making an enslaved person free, while exegetes differ over its sense here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r1.anchor: محررا: اسم مفعول من حرر، ويأتي اختلاف المفسرين في مدلوله في الآية، والتحرير: العتق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p112/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p112/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p112/r5.claim: After mentioning the election of Imran's family, and amid the sūra's discussion of Najran's Christians, the passage recounts the family's beginnings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p112/r5.anchor: لما ذكر أنه تعالى اصطفى آل عمران، وكان معظم صدر هذه السورة في أمر النصارى وفد نجران

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p112/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p112/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p112/r6.claim: Imran's wife was named Hinnah, pronounced with an unpointed ḥāʾ and doubled, open nūn; the name is Hebrew and she was Hinnah daughter of Faqūd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p112/r6.anchor: وامرأة عمران اسمها: حنة، بالحاء المهملة والنون المشددة مفتوحتين وآخرها تاء تأنيث، وهو اسم عبراني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r1.claim: A monastery of Hinnah is known in Syria, and another bears the same name; Abu Nuwas mentions one in a poem.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r1.anchor: يا دير حنة من ذات الاكيداح ... من يصح عنك فإني لست بالصاح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r2.speaker: القرطبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says Hinnah is not known as an Arabic woman's name; Abd al-Ghani ibn Saʿid reports Hinnah, mother of Amr, whose hadith Ibn Jurayj narrates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r2.anchor: وقال القرطبي: لا يعرف في العربي اسم امرأة حنة، وذكر عبد الغني بن سعيد الحافظ: حنة أم عمرو يروي حديثها ابن جريج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r3.claim: Hinnah, Habba, and Hayya are names of people; Khubba is Khubba daughter of Yahya ibn Aktham, mother of Muhammad ibn Nasr; Janna is known only as the name of Dhu al-Rumma's maternal uncle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r3.anchor: ويستفاد حنة مع: حبة، بالحاء المهملة وباء بواحدة من أسفل، و: حية، بالحاء المهملة وياء باثنتين من أسفل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r4.claim: Hinnah not only intended the vow but voiced it to God, first addressing Him as Lord and owner of her and all things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r4.anchor: ولم تكتف حنة بنية النذر حتى أظهرته باللفظ، وخاطبت به الله تعالى، وقدمت قبل التلفظ بذلك نداء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r5.claim: A vow is described as averting feared harm through a self-imposed act of piety; another definition is anything a person obligates upon himself, conditionally or unconditionally.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r5.anchor: وتقدم معنى النذر وهو استدفاع المخوف بما يعقده الإنسان على نفسه من أعمال البر. وقيل: ما أوجبه الإنسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r6.claim: The poetic example uses nadhr for men vowing the speaker's blood and intending to kill him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر: فليت رجالا فيك قد نذروا دمي ... وهموا بقتلي يا بثين لقوني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r7.claim: The lām in laka is causal, with an implied phrase meaning for service of Your sanctuary or for being confined to Your obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r7.anchor: و: لك، اللام فيه لام السبب، وهو على حذف التقدير: لخدمة بيتك، أو للاحتباس على طاعتك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r8.claim: Hinnah made the vow assuming the unborn child would be male, or hoping that the child would be male.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r8.anchor: ما في بطني جزمت النذر على تقدير أن يكون ذكرا، أو لرجاء منها أن يكون ذكرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r9.claim: Muḥarrar means freed from every worldly occupation, from the sense of freedom.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r9.anchor: محررا معناه عتيقا من كل شغل من أشغال الدنيا، فهو من لفظ الحرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r10.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r10.claim: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr explains the vow as dedicating the child to serve the church; Mujahid is also named for this explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r10.anchor: قال محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير: أو خادما للبيعة. قاله مجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r11.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r11.claim: Al-Shaʿbi interprets muḥarrar as devoted exclusively to worship; a report from Khasif attributes this reading to Ikrima and Mujahid as well.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r11.anchor: أو: مخلصا للعبادة، قاله الشعبي. ورواه خصيف عن عكرمة، ومجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r12.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r12.claim: Using mā rather than man is explained either by the unborn child not yet being rational, or because mā is general and may stand for man; the latter explanation is attributed to Sibawayh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r12.anchor: وأتى بلفظ: ما، دون: من، لأن الحمل إذ ذاك لم يتصف بالعقل، أو لأن: ما، مبهمة تقع على كل شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r13.claim: Hinnah asks God to accept her offering; taqabbul is receiving something with approval, originally receiving in return, and here taqabbala functions like the simple verb qabila.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p113/r13.anchor: فتقبل مني دعت الله تعالى بأن يقبل منها ما نذرته له، والتقبل أخذ الشيء على الرضا به، وأصله المقابلة بالجزاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r1.claim: These two attributes fit because Hinnah formed the vow in intention, bound herself by it, uttered it, and prayed for its acceptance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r1.anchor: إنك أنت السميع العليم ختمت بهذين الوصفين لأنها اعتقدت النذر، وعقدته بنيتها، وتلفظت به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r2.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad supply an implied imperative, meaning remember when she said this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r2.anchor: والعامل في: إذ، مضمر تقديره: أذكر، قاله الأخفش، والمبرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj makes the governor the meaning of God's choosing the House of Imran; on this reading the phrase coordinates clauses, since the selection and the woman's speech occur at different times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r3.anchor: أو معنى الاصطفاء، التقدير: واصطفى آل عمران. قاله الزجاج، وعلى هذا يجعل وآل عمران من باب عطف الجمل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r4.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r4.claim: Al-Tabari's analysis, also apparent in al-Zamakhshari, makes samiʿ or samiʿ ʿalīm govern idh because God hears her words and knows her intention.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r4.anchor: وقال الطبري ما معناه: إن العامل فيه: سميع، وهو ظاهر قول الزمخشري، أو: سميع عليم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r5.claim: The author rejects samiʿ as governor: ʿalīm would interrupt between verb and object if a second predicate, or samiʿ would already be adjectival and unable to govern the adverb; moreover God's attributes are not time-limited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r5.anchor: ولا يصح ذلك لأن قوله: عليم، إما أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر، أو وصفا لقوله: سميع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda treats idh as extra, so the meaning is simply that Imran's wife said; the author notes his weakness in grammar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r6.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيدة إلى أن إذ زائدة، المعنى: قالت امرأة عمران. وتقدم له نظير هذا القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r7.claim: Muḥarraran may be a circumstantial accusative from mā, with nadhartu governing it, or from the implied pronoun in the prepositional phrase governed by istaqarra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r7.anchor: وانتصب: محررا، على الحال. قيل: من ما، فالعامل: نذرات. وقيل من الضمير الذي في: استقر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r8.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r8.claim: Makkī analyzes muḥarraran as an adjective for an omitted object, supplying ghulāman muḥarraran.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r8.anchor: وقال مكي فمن نصبه على النعت لمفعول محذوف يقدره: غلاما محررا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya questions the omitted-object analysis because nadhara has already taken mā fī baṭnī as its object; alternatively, muḥarraran may be a verbal noun meaning taḥrīran, supported by poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p114/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وفي هذا نظر، يعني أن: نذر، قد أخذ مفعوله، وهو: ما في بطني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r9.claim: Another view says God accepted Mary in the vow instead of the hoped-for boy and answered her mother's prayer; no girl had previously been accepted as a vow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r9.anchor: وقيل: المعنى فقبلها أي: رضي بها في النذر مكان الذكر في النذر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r6.claim: ما in the vow leaves the unborn child's sex unspecified because the mother cannot see it in the womb, and it applies to either sex.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r6.anchor: والإبهام في قوله: ما في بطني، لما تعذر عليها الاطلاع على ما في بطنها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r7.claim: إنك أنت السميع العليم is emphatic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r7.anchor: والتأكيد في قوله: إنك أنت السميع العليم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r14.claim: The passage contains ellipses at several locations, with some meanings intelligible only when omitted material is supplied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r14.anchor: والحذف في عدة مواضع لا يصح المعنى إلا باعتبارها.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r1.claim: The opening recalls the selection of Imran’s family and explains how that selection occurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r1.anchor: تقرير للاصطفاء وبيان لكيفية والظرف فى حيز النصب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r2.claim: The time clause is the object of an omitted command, meaning ‘remember the time when she said.’
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r2.anchor: أى اذكر لهم وقت قولها وقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r3.claim: An alternative construes the time phrase with the preceding ‘All-Hearing, All-Knowing’ by syntactic competition.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r3.anchor: هو منصوب على الظرفية لما قبله وهو

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r4.claim: Another analysis attaches the time phrase to the implied meaning of ‘He selected,’ joining clause to clause rather than constituent to constituent.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r4.anchor: ظرف لمعنى الاصطفاء المدلول عليه باصطفى المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r5.claim: Imran’s wife is Hanna daughter of Faqūdhā, identified in reports from Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayra; she is Jesus’ maternal grandmother.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r5.anchor: كما رواه إسحق ابن بشر عن ابن عاس رضى الله تعالى عنه والحاكم عن أبى هريرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r6.claim: Al-Alusi cites Ishaq ibn Bishr from Ibn Abbas and al-Hakim from Abu Hurayra for Hanna’s identity.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r6.anchor: كما رواه إسحق ابن بشر عن ابن عاس رضى الله تعالى عنه والحاكم عن أبى هريرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r7.claim: Historians say Hanna’s sister Isha married Zakariya and became Yahya’s mother, making Jesus and Yahya maternal cousins.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r7.anchor: وكان لها أخت اسمها إيشاع تزوجها زكريا عليه الصلاة والسلام هى أم يحيى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r8.claim: The Miʿraj report in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections calls Jesus and Yahya sons of a maternal aunt, which appears to conflict with the cousin relationship.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r8.anchor: ما أخرجه الشيخان فى حديث المعراج من قوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r9.speaker: صاحب التقريب
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r9.claim: The al-Taqrib author explains the Miʿraj wording figuratively: men sometimes call a female cousin ‘aunt’ affectionately, indicating maternal kinship.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r9.anchor: وأجاب صاحب التقريب بأن الحديث مخرج على المجاز فإنه كثيرا ما يطلق الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r10.claim: A competing genealogy makes Isha Hanna’s maternal half-sister and Maryam’s paternal sister, by proposing Imran first married Hanna’s mother and later Hanna.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r10.anchor: وقيل : كانت إيشاع أخت حنة من الام وأخت مريم من الاب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r11.claim: Al-Alusi finds that genealogy weak: it conflicts with the account that Isha and Hanna were both daughters of Faqūdhā and lacks reports for either marriage claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r11.anchor: وفيه أنه مخالف لما ذكره يحيى السنة من أن إيشاع وحنة بنتا فاقوذا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r12.claim: Ibn Asakir transmits from Ibn Abbas that childless, amenorrheic Hanna saw a bird feed its chick, longed for a child, prayed for a son, and menstruated immediately.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r12.anchor: أخرج ابن عساكر عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن حنة امرأة عمران كانت حبست عن الولد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r13.claim: In the same report Hanna vowed the child to sacred service once she believed she was pregnant; only boys were then dedicated, and her husband warned that a girl would not be accepted.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r13.anchor: لئن نجانى الله تعالى ووضعت ما فى بطنى لأجعله محررا ولم يكن يحرر فى ذلك الزمان إلا الغلمان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r14.claim: Because a girl would not qualify for the dedication, Hanna’s vow also implicitly asks God to make the child male, like asking that a servant be freed on one’s behalf.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r14.anchor: وهذا فى الحقيقة استدعاء للولد الذكر لعدم قبول الانثى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r15.claim: Some imams take the wording as emphasizing her vow and changing its conditional form into a direct declaration.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r15.anchor: وجعله بعض الائمة تأكيدا لنذرها وإخراجا له عن صورة التعليق إلى هيئة التنجيز

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r16.claim: The lām of ‘for You’ expresses purpose: the child is dedicated to serving God’s sanctuary.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r16.anchor: واللام من ( لك ) للتعليل ولمراد لخدمة بيتك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas explains muḥarraran as one devoted to temple service, abstaining from worldly affairs and marriage for worship and service of the church.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r17.anchor: والمحرر من يعمل للدنيا ولا يتزوج ويتفرغ لعمل الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r18.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r18.claim: Mujahid glosses muḥarraran as a servant of the church.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r19.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r19.claim: A second report from Mujahid defines the word as pure, with nothing of worldly life mixed into the person.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r19.anchor: وفى رواية عنه الخالص الذى لا يخالطه شئ من أمر الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r20.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r20.claim: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says Hanna meant a person freed and wholly devoted to obedience, not used for her own needs.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r20.anchor: وقال محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير : أرادت عتيقا خالصا لطاعتك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r21.claim: The term derives from freedom in two senses: exemption from enslavement and freedom from base traits and worldly vices.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p133/r21.anchor: وعلى كل هو من الحرية وهى ضربان أن لا يجرى عليه حكم السبى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r1.claim: Muḥarraran is most properly a circumstantial accusative describing mā, governed by ‘I vowed’; the state may be prospective or accompanying.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r1.anchor: وانتصابه على الحالية من ( ما ) والعامل فيه ( نذرت )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r2.claim: Another analysis makes it a circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in ‘for You,’ governed by an implied predicate of existence.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r2.anchor: وقيل : من الضمير الذى فى الجار والمجرور والعامل فيه حينئذ الاستقرار

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan permits reading the form as an accusative verbal noun, taḥrīran, because it conveys the sense of the vow.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r3.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان أن ينصب على المصدر أى تحريرا لانه بمعنى النذر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r4.claim: The emphatic wording signals the abundance of Hanna’s desire for what she is asking.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r4.anchor: وتأكيد الجملة للايذان بوفور الرغبة فى مضمونها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r5.claim: Putting the prepositional phrase first marks her particular concern for God.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r5.anchor: وتقديم الجار والمجرور لكمال الاعتناء به

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r6.claim: The child is called mā to leave its identity and sex indefinite and because it has not reached the rank of rational beings.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r6.anchor: والتعبير عن الولد بما لإبهام أمره وفصوره عن درجة العقلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r7.claim: Taqabbul is to receive something approvingly; its root sense is meeting or requiting with recompense, while here it means to accept.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r7.anchor: و التقبل أخذ الشئ على وجه الرضا وأصله المقابلة بالجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r8.claim: God hears every audible thing and knows what has been and will be, including Hanna’s intention.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r9.claim: God’s knowledge of the sincerity of her intention explains her request for acceptance as a plea for gracious favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r9.anchor: وهو تعليل لاستدعاء القبول من حيث ان علمه تعالى بصحة نيتها وإخلاصها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r10.claim: The emphatic clause displays her firm certainty in what she states.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r10.anchor: وتأكيد الجملة أغرض قوة يقينها بمضمونها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r11.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r11.claim: Restricting hearing and knowledge to God focuses the prayer on Him and cuts off all hope in anything else.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r11.anchor: قاله شيخ الإسلام وتقديم صفة السمع

ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r12.claim: Hearing is mentioned before knowledge because hearing’s innumerable objects are fewer than knowledge’s.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p134/r12.anchor: وتقديم صفة السمع لان متعلقاتها وإن كانت غر متناهية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r22.claim: Hanna’s vow inwardly frees the child from the lower soul’s bondage, making the child sincere in worship and unattached to anything besides God.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r22.anchor: عن رق النفس مخلصا في عبادتك عن الميل إلى السوى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r2.claim: In an inward reading, Imran's wife represents the soul at the first stage of obeying the intellect.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r2.anchor: وهي النفس في أول مراتب طاعتها لعمران العقل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r3.claim: The child vowed in the womb symbolizes the heart, represented as a boy; being freed means owing no servitude to created things.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r3.anchor: محررا ) ليس في رق شئ من المخلوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r1.claim: The Quran’s foretelling of future failures, Byzantine victory, and the Jews’ refusal to wish for death is among its signs beyond human capacity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r1.anchor: والإعلان بالحوادث المستقبلة في الأعصار الآتية كقوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r5.claim: The Quran’s rational coherence and precise meanings unite divine oneness, worship, law, exhortation, instruction, and moral guidance, placing each in its fitting position.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r5.anchor: لأنه اشتمل على توحيد الله تعالى وتنزيهه والدعاء إلى طاعته وبيان طرق عبادته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r6.claim: It joins proof to the claim being proved and uses subtle allusions, symbols, secrets, and wisdom to make obedience and avoidance more compelling.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r6.anchor: جامعا بين الحجة والمحتج له والدليل والمدلول عليه ليكون ذلك أوكد للزوم ما دعا إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r7.claim: The author says the Quran’s distinction from scripture and the Prophet’s non-miraculous speech is as vast as the stars beyond a reaching hand, supporting his poetic comparison.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r8.claim: The common view among most scholars makes the Quran’s supreme eloquence and clarity its central miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r8.anchor: والمشهور عند الجمهور الاقتصار على بلاغته وفصاحته حيث بلغت الرتبة العليا والغاية القصوى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r10.claim: Some scholars say the Quran’s distinctive arrangement is the specific locus of inimitability, while its other miraculous features follow from that form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r10.anchor: وبعضهم جعل المدار النظم المخصوص والباقي تابع له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r12.claim: The author regards the distinctive-arrangement theory as close to the truth, though he signals that it has shortcomings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r12.anchor: وأنت تعلم ما فيه وإن كان قريبا إلى الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r13.claim: He rejects pure ṣarfa as the most remote explanation of inimitability, disapproves al-Murtaḍā’s version, and regards attributing the miracle to the Quran’s pre-eternity as still more remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p32/r13.anchor: وأبعد الأقوال عندي كونه بالصرفة المحضة حتى أن قول المرتضى فيها غير مرتضى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r1.claim: The wife of ʿImran is Hanna daughter of Qafudha, Mary’s mother; this ʿImran is Ibn Mathan, not the father of Moses, with 1,080 years between them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r1.anchor: وهي حنة بنت قافوذا أم مريم، وعمران هو عمران بن ماثان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r2.claim: Another identification gives Mary’s father’s name as ʿImran ibn Ashham.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r3.claim: A vow is something a person makes obligatory upon themself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r3.anchor: والنذر: ما يوجبه الإنسان على نفسه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r4.claim: She dedicated the child as free for God, wholly devoted to worship and temple service, with no worldly occupation; anything sincerely devoted is called muḥarrar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r4.anchor: أي عتيقا خالصا لله مفرغا لعبادة الله ولخدمة الكنيسة لا أشغله بشيء من الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r5.claim: The word also evokes freeing a slave from bondage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r5.anchor: يقال: حررت العبد إذا أعتقته وخلصته من الرق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r6.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others describe the temple dedication: boys served and cleaned the church until puberty, then could choose to stay or leave; only boys were dedicated because girls experienced menstruation and its effects.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي ومحمد بن إسحاق وغيرهما: كان المحرر إذا حرر جعل في الكنيسة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r7.claim: The account says Zakariya and ʿImran married sisters: Ashiya, mother of Yahya, married Zakariya; Hanna, Mary’s mother, married ʿImran. Their family held a high standing with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r7.anchor: وكانت أشياع بنت قافوذا أم يحيى عند زكريا، وكانت حنة بنت قافوذا أم مريم عند عمران

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r8.claim: Hanna had remained childless into old age; seeing a bird feed its chick stirred her longing, and she prayed for a child, vowing to give it to Jerusalem as a temple attendant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r8.anchor: فبينما هي في ظل شجرة بصرت بطائر يطعم فرخا فتحركت بذلك نفسها للولد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r9.claim: After conceiving Mary, Hanna consecrated the child without knowing its sex; ʿImran objected that a girl could not serve, and both were distressed; ʿImran died while she was pregnant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p29#2/r9.anchor: فحملت بمريم فحررت ما في بطنها، ولم تعلم ما هو فقال لها زوجها:

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r5.claim: The accusative of idh is construed through the preceding expression by a contextual relation, or by supplying an imperative “remember.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r5.anchor: فينتصب به إذ على التنازع. وقيل نصبه بإضمار اذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r6.claim: Imran’s wife is Hanne bint Faqūdh, Jesus’ grandmother; Bayḍāwī distinguishes her from the Maryam, daughter of Imran b. Yashhar, who was older than Moses and Aaron, citing Zakariya’s later-era guardianship and family ties.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r6.anchor: وهذه حنة بنت فاقوذ جدة عيسى، وكانت لعمران بن يصهر بنت اسمها مريم أكبر من موسى وهرون فظن أن المراد زوجته ويرده كفالة زكريا

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r7.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r7.claim: A report says Hanne was elderly and barren; seeing a bird feed its chick, she yearned for a child and vowed to dedicate one to the Jerusalem sanctuary, became pregnant with Maryam, and Imran died.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r7.anchor: روي أنها كانت عاقرا عجوزا، فبينما هي في ظل شجرة إذ رأت طائرا يطعم فرخه فحنت إلى الولد وتمنته فقالت: اللهم إن لك علي نذرا إن رزقتني ولدا أن أتصدق به على بيت المقدس فيكون من خدمه، فحملت بمريم وهلك عمران

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r8.claim: Because temple service in their time was reserved for boys, she may have made the vow conditionally or sought a son; muḥarraran means freed for temple service without other work, or sincerely dedicated to worship, and is circumstantial.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r8.anchor: وكان هذا النذر مشروعا في عهدهم للغلمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r9.claim: “Accept from me” asks God to accept the vow she made.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:34-35/r10.claim: God hears her words and knows her intention.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r7.claim: After the preceding selections, the narrative turns to Imran’s family because its central concern is their extraordinary birth and the honor given to Mary.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r7.anchor: ولما كان جل المقصود هنا بيان الكرامات في آل عمران لا سيما في الولادة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r8.claim: إذ introduces a response to people disputing or asking about the family, and the woman is identified as pregnant when she speaks.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r8.anchor: جوابا لمن يجادلك في أمرهم ويسألك عن حالهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r9.claim: Only Jesus receives detailed treatment because the earlier figures introduce his case; the account parallels Adam’s creation in al-Baqara with Jesus’ creation here.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r9.anchor: إنما ذكر توطئة لأمر عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام اختص التفصيل بأمر عيسى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r10.claim: Vowing a child to God was customary among the Israelites, but they expected a son because males served at the sanctuary.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r10.anchor: وكان نذر الولد شائعا في بني إسرائيل إلا أنه كان عندهم معهودا في الذكور لصلاحهم لسدانة بيت الله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r11.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r11.claim: A prophetic report says many men attained perfection, but among women only four did; Mary, daughter of Imran, is named among them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r11.anchor: قال عليه أفضل الصلاة وأزكى السلام ( كمل من الرجال كثير ولم يكمل من النساء إلا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r12.claim: Mary’s mother relinquished her child while still most attached to her in the womb; the account compares this separation with Abraham’s commanded sacrifice of his son at maturity.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r12.anchor: التي لها الإشفاق , فكان الولد أباه فحينئذ يترقى إلى حزب أبيه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r13.claim: The child is dedicated to God, beyond the authority or claims of any created person.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r13.anchor: أي لا اعتراض ولا حكم لأحد من الخلق عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r14.claim: Taḥrīr means seeking freedom; its intensified form conveys firm, complete severance of human guardianship so the child belongs to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r14.anchor: والحرية رفع اليد عن الشيء من كل وجه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r15.claim: She asks for acceptance and grounds the plea in God’s encompassing hearing and knowledge, affirming that these belong to Him alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p69/r15.anchor: عللت سؤالها في التقبل بأن قصرت السمع والعلم عليه سبحانه

DURR-FULL:v2p180/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p180/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Imran's wife as Hinna daughter of Faqudh, Mary's mother; she had been without a child, saw a bird feeding its chick, prayed for a child, conceived, and vowed to dedicate the unborn baby if delivered safely.
DURR-FULL:v2p180/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إن الله اصطفى} يعني اختار من الناس لرسالته

DURR-FULL:v2p180/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p180/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Mathan family were Israelite kings descended from David, and a consecrated child did no worldly work, did not marry, and devoted himself to afterlife worship.
DURR-FULL:v2p180/r8.anchor: وبنو ماثان من ملوك بني إسرائيل من نسل داود والمحرر لا يعمل للدنيا ولا يتزوج

DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.claim: The consecrated child served God and the church; in that period only boys could be dedicated in this way.
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.anchor: يعبد الله تعالى ويكون في خدمة الكنيسة ولم يكن محررا في ذلك الزمان إلا الغلمان

DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r2.claim: Mary's mother told her husband that she had vowed the unborn child to God; he asked how she would fulfill it if the baby were a girl, since girls were considered vulnerable, and she grieved.
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r2.anchor: فقالت لزوجها: ليس جنس من جنس الأنبياء إلا وفيهم محرر غيرنا

DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains her request to God as asking Him to accept what she had vowed.
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r3.anchor: يعني تقبل مني ما نذرت لك

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r4.claim: Ikrima gives Mary's mother's name as Hinna.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: اسم أم مريم حنة

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra says Hinna gave birth to Mary, Jesus's mother.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: حنة ولدت مريم أم عيسى

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Mary's mother vowed to place the child in the church for worship and hoped the child would be a boy.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا} قال: كانت نذرت

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses the vow as dedicating the unborn child to worship.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: نذرت أن تجعله محررا للعبادة

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses muharrar as a servant of the church.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {محررا} قال: خادما للبيعة

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r9.claim: In another report, Mujahid explains muharrar as wholly free of worldly affairs.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {محررا} قال: خالصا لا يخالطه شيء من أمر الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r10.claim: Qatada says only boys were consecrated to stay in the church, serve it, and sweep it; women could not perform this service because of harm, which explains the mother's statement that a male is not like a female.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r10.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: كانت امرأة عمران حررت لله ما في بطنها وكانوا إنما يحررون الذكور

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says she dedicated the child to God and the church so that no one would prevent its worship.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r11.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {محررا} قال: جعلته لله والكنيسة فلا يحال بينه وبين العبادة

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r12.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak describes Israelite custom: a woman nursed her son until he could serve, then gave him to scripture scholars as a consecrated servant.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r12.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: كانت المرأة في زمان بني إسرائيل إذا ولدت غلاما أرضعته

IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ʿImrān's wife vowed that the child in her womb would be placed in the church for worship.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قول الله تعالى اني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا قال : كانت نذرت ان يجعله في الكنيسة يتعبد فيها .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses muḥarraran as devoted to worship, with no worldly concerns mixed into that service.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا قالك للعبادة لا يخالطه شيء من امر الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r3.speaker: عامر الشعبي، سعيد بن جبير، عكرمة، الضحاك، قتادة، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatāda, and al-Suddī are reported with a similar interpretation of muḥarraran as dedicated service.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r3.anchor: روى عن عامر الشعبي ، وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة والضحاك ، وقتادة والسدى ونحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r4.claim: Mujāhid's second view takes muḥarraran to mean a servant of the church; al-Rabīʿ b. Anas and Sharḥabīl b. Saʿd are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p636/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : اني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا قال : خادما للبيعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r1.claim: A temporal opener or prepositional phrase can link a sentence without conjunction; the poem's focus on an event while foregrounding its day illustrates this, and Ibn Ashur prefers this connection for وإذ قالت امرأة عمران, as al-Kashshaf intimates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r1.anchor: فإن مقصده ما حصل في اليوم ، ولكنه جعل الاهتمام بنفس اليوم ، لأنه ظرفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r2.claim: One alternative parses إذ as an accusative dependent on an implicit اذكر, remember.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r2.anchor: وقيل منصوب باذكر ، وقيل متعلق بقوله : { المصير }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r3.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r3.claim: Another proposed attachment is to المصير, but Ibn Ashur considers it remote because of the long separation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r3.anchor: وقيل متعلق بقوله : { المصير } وفيه بعد لطول الفصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r4.claim: Attaching إذ to يحذركم is also remote because the warning has applied since the verse was revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r4.anchor: وقيل بقوله : ( ويحذركم ) وهو بعيد ، لأن التحذير حاصل من وقت نزول الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r5.claim: The temporal phrase should not be governed by a verb in the preceding verse because the resulting discourse does not fit together well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p223/r5.anchor: ولا يحسن أن يجعل عامل الظرف في الآية التي قبل هذه لعدم التئام الكلام حق الالتئام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r12.claim: This is not Imran, father of Moses and Aaron; the passage prepares for the mention of Mary and Jesus, as 3:35 shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r12.anchor: وليس المراد هنا عمران والد موسى وهارون ؛ إذ المقصود هنا التمهيد لذكر مريم وابنها عيسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r13.claim: Mary's father is named Imran ibn Mattan by exegetes; he was a Jewish high priest and righteous man, and the name corresponds to Hebrew Amram.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r13.anchor: فمريم بنت عمران بن ماتان كذا سماه المفسرون ، وكان من أحبار اليهود ، وصالحيهم ، وأصله بالعبرانية عمرام بميم في آخره فهو أبو مريم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r14.speaker: المفسرون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r14.claim: Exegetes say Mary descended from Solomon, but Ibn Ashur rejects this and says her ancestry goes back to Aaron, Moses' brother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r14.anchor: قال المفسرون : هو من نسل سليمان بن داود ، وهو خطأ ، والحق أنه من نسل هارون أخي موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r15.speaker: كتب النصارى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r15.claim: Christian books call Mary's father Joachim; Ibn Ashur suggests this may be a second name, which would be unsurprising.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p230/r15.anchor: وفي كتب النصارى : أن اسمه يوهاقيم ، فلعله كان له اسمان ومثله كثير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة معمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah says idh is extra; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r9.anchor: فقال أبو عبيدة معمر: إذ زائدة، وهذا قول مردود، وقال المبرد والأخفش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r10.speaker: المبرد والأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Akhfash take an implicit verb as the governor of idh, estimated as udhkur, “remember.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r10.anchor: وقال المبرد والأخفش: العامل فعل مضمر تقديره، اذكر إذ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r11.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r11.claim: Al-Zajjāj makes the meaning of God's choosing the governor of idh, effectively “He chose the family of ʿImrān when …”.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p423/r11.anchor: وقال الزجاج: العامل معنى الاصطفاء، التقدير:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r1.claim: On al-Zajjāj's analysis, ʿImrān is excluded from the choosing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وعلى هذا القول يخرج عمران من الاصطفاء، وقال الطبري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r2.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes samiʿ, “hearing,” as the governor of idh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r2.anchor: وقال الطبري ما معناه: إن العامل في إذ قوله سميع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r3.speaker: الطبري عن ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī, transmitting from Ibn Isḥāq, names ʿImrān's wife Ḥannah bint Qādhūdh; she was Maryam's mother.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r3.anchor: وامرأت عمران اسمها حنة بنت قاذوذ فيما ذكر الطبري عن ابن إسحاق، وهي أم مريم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r4.claim: She vows the unborn child to serve God's House in Jerusalem, freed from worldly duties; muḥarraran is a circumstantial accusative from the sense of freedom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r4.anchor: ومعنى قوله: نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا أي جعلت نذرا أن يكون هذا الولد الذي في بطني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r5.claim: Muḥarraran is a circumstantial accusative from ḥurriyyah, freedom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r5.anchor: فهو من لفظ الحرية، ونصبه على الحال، قال مكي:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r6.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r6.claim: Makkī suggests muḥarraran modifies an omitted object, “a boy made free”; Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers this problematic.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r6.anchor: قال مكي: فمن نصبه على النعت لمفعول محذوف يقدره، غلاما محررا، وفي هذا نظر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r7.claim: The House to which the child is vowed is the sanctuary in Jerusalem.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r7.anchor: والبيت الذي نذرته له هو بيت المقدس.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r8.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Ḥannah had long been childless, saw a bird feeding its chick, prayed for a child, conceived Maryam, and vowed her to church service after learning she was pregnant; ʿImrān had died.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r8.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: كان سبب نذر حنة لأنها كانت قد أمسك عنها الولد حتى أسنت فبينما هي في ظل شجرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r9.speaker: مجاهد; الشعبي; سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r9.claim: Mujāhid, al-Shaʿbī, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explain muḥarraran as a servant devoted to the church.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: محررا معناه خادما للكنيسة وقال مثله الشعبي وسعيد بن جبير،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r10.claim: This consecration was customary and obligatory for boys; Ḥannah left the child's sex unstated because it was uncertain, while hoping for a boy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r10.anchor: وكان هذا المعنى من التحرير للكنائس عرفا في الذكور خاصة، وكان فرضا على الأبناء التزام ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r11.claim: She asks God to be pleased with the vow, accept it as a deed, and reward it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r11.anchor: فتقبل مني أي ارض عني في ذلك واجعله فعلا مقبولا مجازى به، والسميع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r12.claim: “The Hearing” points to her prayer and “the Knowing” to her intention.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p424/r12.anchor: والسميع، إشارة إلى دعائها العليم إشارة إلى نيتها.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers Qurʾānic exegesis the noblest science: it grounds the law and other disciplines, accepting what agrees with it and rejecting what conflicts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r1.anchor: فوجدت أمتنها حبالا، وأرسخها جبالا، وأجملها آثارا، وأسطعها أنوارا، علم كتاب الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r2.claim: He says Qurʾānic study most directly draws one near to God, purifies intentions, restrains wrongdoing, and encourages good deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r2.anchor: وأيقنت أنه أعظم العلوم تقريبا إلى الله تعالى، وتخليصا للنيات، ونهيا عن الباطل، وحضا على الصالحات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r3.claim: He hopes for salvation through sustained engagement with Qurʾānic meanings, recitation, and composition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r3.anchor: ورجوت أن الله تعالى يحرم على النار فكرا عمرته أكثر عمره معانيه، ولسانا مرن على آياته ومثانيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites the Prophetic injunction to write down knowledge as the reason he began recording exegetical insights.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r4.anchor: وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «قيدوا العلم بالكتاب» ففزعت إلى تعليق ما يتخيل لي في المناظرة من علم التفسير وترتيب المعاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r5.claim: He aims for a concise, edited, comprehensive commentary, including stories only when a verse requires them and attributing scholars’ explanations as the early generations received them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r5.anchor: وقصدت فيه أن يكون جامعا وجيزا محررا، لا أذكر من القصص إلا ما لا تنفك الآية إلا به، وأثبت أقوال العلماء في المعاني منسوبة إليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r6.claim: He rejects interpretations that distort sound Arabic through heretical symbols or esoteric claims, and flags problematic language even from otherwise trusted scholars.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r6.anchor: كتاب الله من مقاصده العربية السليمة من إلحاد أهل القول بالرموز، وأهل القول بعلم الباطن، وغيرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r7.claim: He orders commentary around the verse’s legal, grammatical, lexical, semantic, and reading issues, tracing its words and recording established and anomalous readings and possible meanings concisely.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p34/r7.anchor: وسردت التفسير في هذا التعليق بحسب رتبة ألفاظ الآية من حكم، أو نحو، أو لغة، أو معنى، أو قراءة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r1.claim: Abu ʿUbayda and Ibn Qutayba take idh as extra rather than syntactically essential.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r1.anchor: في إذ قولان أحدهما أنها زائدة واختاره أبو عبيدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r2.speaker: المبرد، الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Akhfash take the clause to mean “remember when the wife of ʿImran said.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r2.anchor: أحدها أن المعنى اذكر إذ قالت امرأة عمران قاله المبرد والأخفش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj makes idh governed by God's choosing: He chose the family of ʿImran when she spoke and chose them when the angels spoke to Mary.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r3.anchor: معنى الاصطفاء فيكون المعنى اصطفى آل عمران

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r4.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir al-Tabari makes the clause depend on samīʿ, meaning God heard her when she said this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r4.anchor: والثالث أنها من صلة سميع تقديره والله سميع إذ قالت وهذا اختيار ابن جرير الطبري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies ʿImran's wife as Hanna, Mary's mother; this ʿImran was ibn Matan, not the father of Moses, Mary was not Moses' sister, and Jesus lived 1,800 years after Moses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس واسم امرأة عمران حنة وهي أم مريم وهذا عمران بن ماتان وليس عمران أبي موسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r6.claim: Muḥarraran means freed from worldly servitude and dedicated to worship; Ibn Qutayba says aʿtaqtu al-ghulām and ḥarrartuhu both mean “I freed the boy.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r6.anchor: والمحرر العتيق قال ابن قتيبة يقال أعتقت الغلام وحررته سواء وأرادت أي نذرت أن أجعل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says parents in their community could bind their children to obey a vow, so a father might vow that his son serve in a sanctuary.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج كان على اولادهم فرضا أن يطيعوهم في نذرهم فكان الرجل ينذر في ولده أن يكون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r8.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the childless Hanna, already advanced in age, saw a bird feeding its chick and prayed for a child, vowing to dedicate it to the sanctuary at Jerusalem; she conceived Mary and ʿImran died during her pregnancy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن اسحاق كان السبب في نذرها أنه أمسك عنها الولد حتى أسنت فرأت طائرا يطعم فرخا له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r9.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r9.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Yaʿla says an equivalent vow is valid in Islamic law when a parent vows to raise a young child in worship and teach Qur'an, jurisprudence, and religious sciences.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p376#2/r9.anchor: قال القاضي أبو يعلى والنذر في مثل ما نذرت صحيح في شريعتنا فانه إذا نذر الإنسان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p33#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p33#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p33#2/r1.claim: The wife of Imran is Mary’s mother, Hanna daughter of Faqudh.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p33#2/r1.anchor: امرأة عمران هذه أم مريم [بنت عمران] (5) عليها السلام (6) وهي حنة بنت فاقوذ،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p33#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p33#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
